vulns.title: Drupal says core access-bypass flaw CVE-2026-136716 (SA-CORE-2026-019) is being exploited in the wild
vulns.desc: Drupal says attackers are already exploiting a serious flaw in its core software. Sites that left the installer reachable after the earlier advisory may still have been compromised.
vulns.action: Drupal advises updating to the fixed version for your release line and running update.php, securing the installer, and checking logs for unauthorized access, especially to the user 1 account.

vulns.title: D-Link R32 firmware 1.10B02 has three remote OS command injection flaws (CVE-2026-136821, -136822, -136823); public exploits reported
vulns.desc: Three flaws in D-Link R32 router firmware 1.10B02 let a remote attacker run operating-system commands. The listings say exploits are public and name no fix; no D-Link statement was shown.
vulns.action: General advice: restrict remote access to the R32's management interface; the pages list no vendor fix, so check D-Link's own advisory for one.

vulns.title: D-Link R32 firmware 1.10B02 has three remote OS command injection flaws (CVE-2026-136821, -136822, -136823); public exploits reported

vulns.title: ThaiCERT warns of code injection in binary-parser for Node.js (CVE-2026-134814), versions before 2.3.1
vulns.desc: ThaiCERT says a Node.js library, binary-parser, can be made to run an attacker's JavaScript if untrusted input defines the parser. Versions before 2.3.1 are affected.
vulns.action: ThaiCERT advises updating to binary-parser 2.3.1 or later, including transitive dependencies, and not letting untrusted input set parser options such as length, key, tag or offset.

vulns.title: AWS bulletin: input validation flaw CVE-2026-134070 in Config remediation runbook for Session Manager audit logs
vulns.desc: AWS says a crafted value in one of its Config remediation runbooks could let a permitted user inject settings, including commands, into Session Manager preferences. Revisions created before October 22, 2026 are affected.
vulns.action: AWS recommends upgrading to the fixed revision, patching forked code and updating pinned automations, State Manager associations and AWS Config remediations.

vulns.title: Compass Security details Pwn2Own Tokyo 2026 unauthenticated root code execution in Alpine iLX-F511 infotainment system
vulns.desc: Researchers showed that someone on the same network could run code as root on an Alpine iLX-F511 car infotainment unit. ZDI's advisory lists no patch.
vulns.action: ZDI's advisory advises restricting interaction with the product; it lists no vendor fix.

vulns.title: ZDI publishes 0-day advisory ZDI-26-1044 on GNU Inetutils FTP client command injection (CVE-2026-136613)
vulns.desc: ZDI says the GNU Inetutils FTP client can be made to run an attacker's code if a user connects to a malicious FTP server. ZDI rates it CVSS 7.5 and suggests limiting use of the product.
vulns.action: ZDI's advisory lists restricting interaction with the product as the mitigation.

vulns.title: Windows Remote Access API flaw CVE-2026-119853: Core Security exploit module reported for local privilege escalation to SYSTEM
vulns.desc: A Windows flaw lets someone who already runs code on a PC raise their rights to SYSTEM, Tenable and Cyber Press say. Cyber Press reports Microsoft shipped fixes for 28 affected Windows products.
vulns.action: General advice: install the Microsoft November 2026 Windows updates that fix CVE-2026-119853 (Cyber Press lists KB5131077, KB5131080 and KB5131085).

vulns.title: Volans NGFW r5.1 SSLVPN client flaw CVE-2026-135797 allows remote OS command injection; CVE record says exploit is public
vulns.desc: A flaw in the SSLVPN client page of the Volans r5.1 firewall lets a remote attacker inject operating-system commands. The CVE record says an exploit is public and lists no fix; the vendor did not respond.
vulns.action: General advice: no vendor fix is listed in the CVE record; restrict access to the firewall's SSLVPN and management interfaces and watch for vendor updates.

vulns.title: Tenda RX3 router command-injection flaw CVE-2026-136549 has a public proof of concept, ZeroPath says
vulns.desc: ZeroPath says a public proof of concept exists for a command-injection flaw in the Tenda RX3 router, and that no fixed firmware is established.
vulns.action: General advice: if you run a Tenda RX3 on firmware 16.03.13.11_multi, restrict or disable remote web management until Tenda publishes a fix.

vulns.title: Symfony fixes code-execution flaw in stimulus-bridge build loader (CVE-2026-133780)
vulns.desc: Symfony says a build tool in its Stimulus package could be tricked by a crafted comment into running code on a developer or build machine. Version 4.0.3 fixes it.
vulns.action: Symfony advises upgrading @symfony/stimulus-bridge to 4.0.3 or later.

vulns.title: SolarWinds publishes fixes for critical Serv-U privilege escalation flaws, including CVE-2026-123172
vulns.desc: SolarWinds says several serious flaws in its Serv-U file transfer software are fixed in a new release. The advisories read do not mention attacks.
vulns.action: SolarWinds advises updating to Serv-U 2026.4, the fixed version named in its advisories (affected: 2026.3 and below).

vulns.title: ZDI advisory: RustDesk Client for Windows reg_recovery local privilege escalation (CVE-2026-131827), fixed by vendor
vulns.desc: A flaw in RustDesk's Windows client lets someone who already runs low-privileged code gain SYSTEM rights. ZDI says RustDesk has issued an update.
vulns.action: ZDI points to RustDesk's update, described in GitHub pull request #17040, as the fix.

vulns.title: rsyslog omdtls name and fingerprint modes do not verify DTLS server identity (CVE-2026-132145)
vulns.desc: The advisory says a log-forwarding setting in rsyslog could send logs to the wrong server if an attacker can redirect the traffic. It says this is not the default setup, and a fix is out.
vulns.action: The advisory says to update to the 2026-11-24 daily stable and, where the network target differs from the certificate identity, set tls.permittedpeer explicitly after updating.

vulns.title: ZDI publishes 0-day advisory on PyTorch torch_save_to_dcp deserialization flaw
vulns.desc: ZDI says a checkpoint conversion tool in PyTorch can run attacker code when a user opens a malicious file. ZDI says the vendor treated it as expected behavior, and its page lists no patch.
vulns.action: ZDI advises restricting interaction with the product; its page lists no patch.

vulns.title: ZDI publishes 0-day advisory on PyTorch PT2 file parsing code execution (ZDI-26-1056)
vulns.desc: ZDI disclosed a flaw in how PyTorch opens PT2 files that could let an attacker run code if a user opens a malicious file. ZDI says the vendor called it expected behavior and the advisory names no patch.
vulns.action: ZDI's only stated mitigation is to restrict interaction with the product; the advisory names no vendor patch.

vulns.title: ZDI publishes 0-day advisory on pip configuration file permissions (ZDI-26-1066)
vulns.desc: ZDI disclosed a flaw in the Python tool pip where configuration file permissions could let a local attacker gain higher privileges. ZDI says the vendor rejected the report and names no fix.
vulns.action: ZDI's only stated mitigation is to restrict interaction with the product; the advisory names no vendor patch.

vulns.title: Panabit Smart Application Gateway flaw CVE-2026-135790 allows remote OS command injection; public exploit reported, no vendor reply
vulns.desc: A flaw in the Panabit Smart Application Gateway lets a remote attacker run operating-system commands. The CVE record says exploit code is public and the vendor did not respond.
vulns.action: General advice: restrict access to the gateway's web interface and watch for a Panabit fix; the CVE record names no patch.

vulns.title: Mozilla fixes Thunderbird flaws, including a Critical OpenPGP sender-spoofing bug (MFSA 2026-134)
vulns.desc: Mozilla released a Thunderbird update with security fixes, including one rated Critical that could make a signed email appear to come from a different sender.
vulns.action: Mozilla's advisory names the fixed Thunderbird version; the Saudi National Cybersecurity Authority's alert encourages users to review the advisory and apply the updates.

vulns.title: MediaWiki EditAccount extension flaw CVE-2026-132669: reported unauthenticated account takeover
vulns.desc: A MediaWiki add-on called EditAccount can, according to a Wikimedia task, let anyone who is not logged in reset the password or email of any account, including admins.
vulns.action: SecurityContext advises updating to the latest version of the EditAccount extension; the Wikimedia task says the issue was added to the next supplemental security release.

vulns.title: ZDI publishes authenticated remote code execution flaw in LiteLLM pass-through endpoints (CVE-2026-136539), labelled Pwn2Own
vulns.desc: ZDI says a logged-in attacker could run code on LiteLLM servers through a flaw in pass-through endpoints. ZDI says LiteLLM has released an update.
vulns.action: ZDI says LiteLLM released an update to fix the flaw; apply the vendor's update.

vulns.title: Joomla fixes missing authentication in the web installer (CVE-2026-123214) in versions 5.4.11 and 6.2.1
vulns.desc: Joomla says the installer of an already installed site can still be used by anyone to change the site's configuration. Joomla has released fixed versions.
vulns.action: Joomla advises upgrading to version 5.4.11 or 6.2.1.

vulns.title: Joomla 5.4.11 and 6.2.1 fix RCE through media custom field parameters (CVE-2026-129393)
vulns.desc: Joomla says a flaw in how media field parameters are escaped could let an attacker run code on the site. Joomla's advisory says to upgrade to 5.4.11 or 6.2.1.
vulns.action: Joomla advises upgrading to 5.4.11 or 6.2.1.

vulns.title: Joomla 5.4.11 and 6.2.1 fix webservice ACL, Schema.org plugin and GET request task plugin flaws
vulns.desc: Joomla released versions 5.4.11 and 6.2.1 that fix three information-exposure flaws, including content that could be read without the right permission. Joomla's advisories say to upgrade.
vulns.action: Joomla advises upgrading to version 5.4.11 or 6.2.1.

vulns.action: The Hacker News reports users are advised to update GeoServer to 2.27.7, 2.28.6 or 3.0.2 as soon as possible.

vulns.desc: Flatpak, the Linux app packaging system, has released 1.18.6 to fix two flaws that a malicious app could use to gain root-owned files or break out of its sandbox. Older releases are assumed to be affected.
vulns.action: The Flatpak advisory says to upgrade to Flatpak 1.18.6; older LTS distributions can backport the fixes, and Linuxiac says to update once your distribution ships patched packages.

vulns.action: INCIBE-CERT reports the manufacturer replaced dynamic query construction with parameterised queries and strengthened PIN and QR code validation; apply the manufacturer's fixed version.

vulns.desc: Debian released a runc update fixing three flaws that, per its advisory, could expose host resources, cause denial of service or allow escape from a container.
vulns.action: Debian recommends upgrading runc packages; on Debian stable (trixie) the fixed version is 1.1.15+ds1-2+deb13u1.

vulns.desc: CISA warns of a serious flaw in Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controllers that a remote attacker could trigger without logging in. Danfoss plans a fix in an upcoming 5.5.x release; no exploitation had been reported to CISA.
vulns.action: CISA advises minimising network exposure, keeping control systems off the internet and behind firewalls, and using updated VPNs for remote access; Danfoss plans to fix this in AK-SM 800A software 5.5.x.

vulns.title: D-Link DIR-X1860 4.5.2 flaw CVE-2026-135788 allows remote OS command injection in anweb; public exploit reported
vulns.desc: A flaw in the D-Link DIR-X1860 router firmware 4.5.2 lets a remote attacker run operating-system commands. The listing says exploit code is public and shows no D-Link fix.
vulns.action: General advice: restrict remote access to the router; CVE Feed's page also lists updating the firmware and validating user inputs as mitigations.

vulns.title: CERT@VDE advisory VDE-2026-154: four vulnerabilities in CODESYS Visualization
vulns.desc: Four flaws in CODESYS Visualization, used with industrial controllers, were published. The advisory says three could let a malicious runtime or an interceptor run functions on an engineering workstation.
vulns.action: CERT@VDE advises updating CODESYS Visualization to version 4.11.0.0, enabling encrypted online communication between the CODESYS Development System and Control runtime, and using only trusted CODESYS projects.

vulns.desc: ZDI says the ssh service on the ChargePoint Home Flex home EV charger uses hard-coded credentials, so someone on the same network can get in without a login. The advisory lists a firmware fix.
vulns.action: ZDI's advisory lists the fix as Home Flex firmware version 2024.02.00.259-alpha.

vulns.title: ZDI publishes 0-day advisory for BusyBox ftpd directory traversal (CVE-2026-136442)
vulns.desc: ZDI has published details of a flaw in the BusyBox FTP server that, it says, lets unauthenticated remote attackers create or delete files or disclose information. The page records no vendor response.
vulns.action: ZDI advises restricting interaction with the product, given the nature of the flaw.

vulns.title: Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0011 fixes 23 vulnerabilities across VMware products, including ESX and vCenter
vulns.desc: Broadcom fixed 23 VMware flaws, including a critical vCenter login bypass. Rapid7 says a public proof-of-concept exploit works and recommends urgent patching.
vulns.action: Rapid7 recommends remediating exposed systems on an urgent basis outside of normal patching cycles; Broadcom's advisory VMSA-2026-0011 lists the fixed version for each product, and for ESX and vCenter 7.0 contact Broadcom support.

vulns.title: Apache Karaf CVE-2026-129959: SFTP/SCP on the SSH port bypasses the command ACL
vulns.desc: A flaw in Apache Karaf lets a low-privileged logged-in user read sensitive files and add code through file transfer on the SSH port. The advisory says it is fixed in 4.4.13 and 4.5.0.
vulns.action: Apache advises upgrading to Karaf 4.4.13 or 4.5.0; if SFTP/SCP is not needed, set sftpEnabled=false in etc/org.apache.karaf.shell.cfg and restart.

vulns.title: Acer Connect M6E 5G router flaw CVE-2026-9790 exposes API endpoints without authentication; Acer urges patching
products: Acer Connect M6E 5G Portable WiFi Router
vulns.desc: A flaw in the Acer Connect M6E 5G portable router lets devices on its WiFi reach some API endpoints without logging in. The CVE record rates it critical and says Acer recommends updating the firmware immediately.
vulns.action: Acer advises applying firmware M6E_GBL_1.00.000107, delivered over the air, immediately.

vulns.title: Zstandard information-disclosure flaw CVE-2026-124851 fixed in 1.6.0, oss-security post says
vulns.desc: A flaw in the Zstandard compression library can let crafted input make the output reveal internal memory. A fixed version, 1.6.0, is out; the post reports no attacks.
vulns.action: The oss-security post advises upgrading to Zstandard 1.6.0.

vulns.title: Patchstack: WP Rocket plugin before 3.24.2 has unauthenticated remote code execution flaw (CVE-2026-125812)
vulns.desc: A serious flaw in the WP Rocket WordPress plugin could let an attacker with no login run code on a site, according to Patchstack. Zeropath says an update is available.
vulns.action: Patchstack advises updating WP Rocket to version 3.24.2 or later as an immediate action; it says it has issued a mitigation rule to block attacks until the plugin is updated.

vulns.desc: WHMCS, billing software used by web hosts, released updates for several flaws. One could let anyone who can load the shopping cart read customer data and admin password hashes, according to The Hacker News.
vulns.action: WHMCS advises updating to the fixed releases (9.1.2, 9.0.10 or 8.13.8); per The Hacker News, WHMCS Cloud updates automatically.

vulns.action: WAGO advises (per CERT@VDE) updating to firmware 4.10.0 (FW32) or higher; for custom firmware, contact WAGO support.

vulns.action: General advice: securitycontext.com says to update to the latest version, but names no fixed version; check TOTOLINK's site for a firmware update.

vulns.title: nginx 1.30.8 and 1.31.10 fix excessive CPU usage flaw when ssl_early_data is used (CVE-2026-132779)
vulns.desc: The nginx project released new versions that fix a flaw that can make the web server use excessive processor time when the ssl_early_data setting is on.
vulns.action: nginx.org's release announces 1.30.8 (stable) and 1.31.10 (mainline) as the fixed versions; update to them.

vulns.title: INCIBE-CERT: default credentials in Danfoss AK-SC and AK-SM refrigeration controllers (CVE-2026-127057)
vulns.desc: INCIBE-CERT warns that two older Danfoss refrigeration controllers use default passwords from their manuals. Someone who can reach the login page could change temperature or alarm settings. No patch exists for these models.
vulns.action: INCIBE-CERT advises removing management interfaces exposed on public IP addresses from the internet, allowing remote maintenance only through a secure VPN or protected network, using strong unique passwords instead of default or shared ones, and planning replacement of the two models with the newer

vulns.title: HKCERT: F5 BIG-IP affected by remote code execution flaw CVE-2026-126714; proof-of-concept code public
vulns.desc: Hong Kong's cyber security centre warns that F5 BIG-IP network devices have a flaw that could let a logged-in attacker run commands, and that test attack code is public.

vulns.title: Elastic advisory: Elasticsearch LZ4 transport over-read CVE-2026-82303 can leak data from other requests
vulns.desc: A flaw in how Elasticsearch decompresses network traffic between servers can let a remote attacker read data from outside their own request. Elastic has released fixed versions.
vulns.action: Elastic advises upgrading to 8.19.24, 9.4.9 or 9.5.6; until then keep transport ports private, enforce mutual TLS and restrict source addresses.

vulns.title: Cribl discloses CVE-2026-115899, code injection in Cribl Stream REST Collector pagination (CVSS 9.3)

vulns.action: Cribl advises: "Upgrade Cribl Stream to version 4.21.0 or later."

vulns.title: Google fixes Chrome flaw CVE-2026-134401 rated critical, Cyber Security News reports
vulns.desc: Google updated desktop Chrome to fix a flaw rated critical. Cyber Security News says a crafted web page could let an attacker run code outside the browser's boundary; no attacks are indicated.
vulns.action: GovCERT.HK advises updating Google Chrome to version 158.0.8127.88 or later, via auto-update or About Google Chrome, then relaunching the browser.

vulns.title: Zeropath: AutoGPT Platform 0.6.26 through 0.7.4 has hardcoded default JWT key allowing authentication bypass (CVE-2026-130169)
vulns.desc: AutoGPT Platform shipped with a built-in default signing key for login tokens, which Zeropath says lets an attacker bypass authentication. Zeropath says a fixed version is out and proof-of-concept code is public.
vulns.action: Zeropath advises upgrading to AutoGPT Platform 0.8.0 or later, checking whether JWT_VERIFY_KEY and SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET are set to the default value, and reviewing logs for HS256 Bearer tokens.

advisory.name: CVE-2026-0322 PAN-OS: Authenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE) in the Management Interface

check: Affected PAN-OS 12.2: below 12.2.4. 12.1: below 12.1.4-h12, 12.1.7-h8 or 12.1.10-h2 (by train).
No special configuration is required to be affected. PA-Series, VM-Series and Panorama are affected; Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not.
Check whether the management interface is reachable from untrusted networks; the advisory says risk is highest when it is reachable from the internet.
workaround: No known workarounds exist, per the advisory.

Threat IDs 510046 and 510047 (content 9159-10287 or later) give partial protection and need SSL Decryption.

Best-practice options linked from the advisory: route inbound management traffic through a data-plane port, replace the certificate, decrypt inbound management traffic, enable Threat Prevention on it.

advisory.name: GPUStack GHSA-gj9m-f8ph-pmhr: Authentication bypass via trusted loopback source

check: Affected: gpustack (pip) versions below 2.2.0.
Default force_auth_localhost is False; a same-host reverse proxy using proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:<port> makes every remote request arrive as loopback.
The advisory gives no dedicated check procedure; compare your version with 2.2.0 and review the proxy configuration.
workaround: Set force_auth_localhost=true.
Make sure the proxy cannot make external traffic appear as loopback, and strip any client-supplied X-GPUStack-Real-IP header at the edge.
Keep the API off untrusted networks (VPN or edge authentication).
compromise_signs: Advisory reports exploitation in the wild against a v2.1.1 deployment: attacker-created custom backends running reverse shells.
Attackers could mint persistent admin API keys with scope ["*"].

advisory.name: PHP Security Advisory: 21 October 2026 (Critical RCE Vulnerabilities)

check: Affected: all PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. The advisory gives no explicit version ranges.
Risk is highest with mod_php, where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs.
PHP 8.1 and older no longer receive updates from the PHP project; ask your distribution or LTS vendor for backported fixes.
The advisory gives no version-check command. Compare your PHP branch against the fixed versions listed.
fixed: 7.4, 8.0, 8.1: minimal source backports in php-src branches named PHP-<version>-CVE-2026-109618-109619; distributions may ship patches
workaround: Updating is the complete fix; the mitigations reduce exposure but do not make an installation safe.

Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 in php.ini, an FPM pool or server config that applies before request parsing, and restart every worker. Do not rely on ini_set() or .user.ini. This blocks only the confirmed session paths.
On PHP 8.5, set fatal_error_backtraces=0 and restart every worker. This blocks only the confirmed fatal backtrace path.
Remove invalid or deprecated settings applied per request that emit diagnostics before initialization; hiding diagnostics with error_reporting, display_errors or @ does not help.
Fix attacker-reachable fatal errors and execution timeouts, including failures in callbacks, upload or import processing and cleanup.
compromise_signs: The PHP advisory lists no indicators of compromise.

advisory.name: FreeSWITCH GHSA-mg63-h38w-8p9p: inbound SIP MESSAGE runs API commands

check: Affected: FreeSWITCH 1.11.2 and earlier.

Vulnerable configuration: any SIP profile that accepts inbound MESSAGE, which is the default. Chat is on unless a profile sets enable-chat=false; stock conf/vanilla leaves it on for the internal and external profiles.
The advisory gives no version-check command.
fixed: FreeSWITCH 1.11.3 and later (adds per-profile enable-chat-api-proto, off by default; upgrading is the complete remedy)
workaround: Set enable-chat=false on every profile that does not need inbound SIP chat (this disables all inbound MESSAGE chat delivery on that profile).
Enabling auth-messages alone is not enough; also remove directory users that lack a password or a1-hash, such as default in conf/vanilla/directory/default/default.xml.
Setting disable_system_api_commands=true removes only the system API; the route stays open to other APIs.
compromise_signs: The advisory lists no indicators; it states exploitation has been observed in the wild. The fixed version logs rejected requests with source and requested command, which may help review.

advisory.name: Check Point sk1000362: local privilege escalation to root via the dynamic_server socket (CVSS 7.8)

check: Affected products: Force Firewalls, Management and Log Servers, Multi-Domain Security Management and Multi-Domain Log Server, Maestro Orchestrator, versions R82.20, R82.10, R82, R81.20, R81.10, R81. Not affected: Spark Firewalls and Smart-1 Cloud.
Run ls -l /tmp/dynamic_socket: a fixed system shows srw-rw---- root config (0660); srwxrwxrwx (0777) means it is exposed.
In Expert mode, ps auxw | grep -v grep | grep 'dynamic_server' shows whether the dynamic_server process is running.
The attacker needs local code execution on the appliance first.
fixed: R82.20: Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator Take 14 or later
R81.10 and R81: no fix listed (both end of support)
workaround: Stop dynamic_server and keep it from restarting with dbset process:dynamic_server followed by dbset :save (see the advisory for the exact value to set). This breaks the Dynamic CLI commands in sk144112; to re-enable run dbset process:dynamic_server t then dbset :save.
compromise_signs: The daemon logs every command it receives to /var/log/dynamicCli.log. Legitimate requests carry a specific Clish wrapper; commands received without it may mean a root command ran through the socket.
Use of the system() sink (Received = #return_value#) is uncommon in legitimate traffic.
Received commands containing id, whoami, /etc/shadow, ncat, nc, /dev/tcp, curl, wget, base64, useradd or authorized_keys indicate exploitation attempts.
On fixed systems, 'Rejected connection from unauthorized uid' entries show blocked attempts; a non-zero or unexpected UID means an escalation attempt was blocked.

advisory.name: Alpine Linux: openssh-server password authentication bypass (2026-11-05)

check: Alpine says you are affected if all hold: openssh-server built without PAM (or openssh-server-pam with UsePAM no), and PasswordAuthentication yes (the default unless changed).

An account has the password field "*" (for example root:* in Alpine base images since about 3.16, key-only users, tiny-cloud images' alpine user), and at least one local account has a $5$ or $6$ hash.
Not affected per Alpine: openssh-server-pam with UsePAM yes, PasswordAuthentication no, locked (!) accounts.
The OpenSSH 10.6p2 release notes describe the same bug for some Linux systems built and run with PAM support disabled. Neither page printed this CVE number; the CVE link comes from CISA's KEV record.
fixed: After upgrading run: apk upgrade -U -a, then rc-service sshd restart (upgrading alone does not restart the daemon)
workaround: Disable password logins: mkdir -p /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d, then echo 'PasswordAuthentication no' > /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-no-passwords.conf
Validate and restart with: sshd -t && rc-service sshd restart; confirm with: sshd -T | grep -i passwordauthentication (expect passwordauthentication no)
Before starting, make sure SSH key login works and keep your current session open.
compromise_signs: In /var/log/messages look for sshd lines reading "Accepted password for" an account that has no password, such as alpine, root or any key-only user.
Review doas use, recently created users, files and authorized keys on exposed machines; Alpine says if you cannot rule out a login, treat the machine as compromised.

advisory.name: VSA-2026-062: Empty-object login token (Vates)

check: Affected: Xen Orchestra before 6.9.2 (stable) and before 6.10.1 (latest), and the Xen Orchestra Appliance.
Monitor HTTP requests for authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D or authenticationToken=j:{}. The advisory says unauthenticated access leaves no log entry.
In Xen Orchestra, look for a running VM named 'pivot2'.
On XCP-ng hosts run: xe vm-list params=name-label,platform | grep -B1 'hvm_serial: file'
On XCP-ng hosts run: zgrep -- '-serial file:' /var/log/xensource.log*
On XCP-ng hosts run: ls -la /etc/ld.so.preload /.ustar* /etc/cron.d/zz-ustar*
fixed: Installs from source: update to the latest master
workaround: Do not expose Xen Orchestra to the internet; put it on a dedicated management network.
Block the IP addresses and the Tor onion address the advisory lists, for ingress and egress.
Add a WAF or reverse-proxy rule matching the empty-token patterns; the advisory cautions that regex rules can be bypassed with other formats.
compromise_signs: Requests carrying the empty-object authenticationToken patterns.
A VM named 'pivot2'.
VMs with hvm_serial: file set, or "-serial file:" entries in the xensource logs.
Files /etc/ld.so.preload, /.ustar* and /etc/cron.d/zz-ustar* on XCP-ng hosts.
The advisory says these cover only the identified campaign; their absence does not prove no compromise.

advisory.name: CVE-2026-21589 Arbitrary File Access Vulnerability Impacts Multiple Products

check: All versions before the fixed versions are affected. The advisory has no separate check; compare the installed version with the list.

workaround: Remove the instance from the internet until patched or mitigated.
WAF or proxy rule blocking URLs with '..' next to '/', backslash or '::', including URL-encoded forms.

advisory.name: Cisco cisco-sa-asaftd-tunnel-dos-s6mgkb75: ASA and FTD SSL VPN denial of service

check: Vulnerable when the running config contains webvpn with SSL VPN enabled on at least one interface (enable <interface_name>).
And secondary authentication is configured in a tunnel group: look for secondary-authentication-server-group under every tunnel group, including DefaultWEBVPNGroup.
Removing tunnel-group-list enable does not remove the exposure, because the default group still exposes the issue.
On FTD, review the remote access VPN policy in FMC or FDM and the resulting running config.
Not affected: Cloud-delivered Firewall, cdFMC, Secure Access, Secure FMC Software.
workaround: Cisco states there are no workarounds but describes a temporary mitigation. Case 1: if DefaultWEBVPNGroup does not use secondary authentication, run 'no tunnel-group-list enable' in WebVPN mode (users must then know the connection profile name).

advisory.name: PaperCut NG/MF bulletin 27 Aug 2026: Authentication Bypass

fixed: Version 23 and earlier: no emergency patches or maintenance releases; upgrade to 24, 25 or 26
check: The bulletin says it applies to all versions of PaperCut NG and PaperCut MF; compare your build with the fixed builds listed.
Emergency patch builds show the same version number as the unpatched release, so the in-product notice cannot tell them apart; installing a maintenance release clears it.
Patch Site Servers and secondary/print servers as well as the primary Application Server.
The bulletin gives no console path or command for checking exposure.
workaround: Until upgraded, restrict web access to the Application Server to trusted addresses only.
Emergency Patch Release 3 is listed as mitigating this CVE, but the maintenance releases replace all emergency patches and are the recommended build.
compromise_signs: Alerts from IDS, endpoint or network tools involving the Application Server, especially suspicious activity from pc-app.exe.
Missing, truncated or deleted PaperCut server.log files.
server.log entries reporting a database driver lookup failure for an invalid JDBC URL, or database errors looking up a card ID with odd values; the bulletin lists exact strings.
A .class file in the server lib folder, and a .cmd and a .out file in the server data\content folder (the attacker may remove them).
pc-app.exe launching cmd.exe for discovery commands, then PowerShell downloads; a "Remote Access Service" service (LocalSystem, JWrapper-Remote Access path) or unexpected AnyDesk installs.

The bulletin says absence of these indicators does not prove a system was not affected. For suspected compromise: secure current backups, wipe and rebuild the Application Server, restore a clean backup from before suspicious activity.

CVE-2015-3306.exploitation_status: Known exploited: CISA added it to KEV on 8 Oct 2026 (due 11 Oct). Public exploit code has been reported since April 2015. No named attacker in the sources read.
CVE-2015-3306.how_exploited: An access-control flaw in ProFTPD's optional mod_copy module. In ProFTPD 1.3.5 the module's site copy commands could be used before login, so anyone who can reach the FTP port can copy files from any location the server process can read to any location it can write. That lets an attacker read sensitive files by copying them somewhere they can fetch, or plant files. On a host that also runs a web server able to run PHP, a planted file in the web folder becomes arbitrary command execution as the web server user (SAINT; Debian notes possible code execution).
preconditions: The FTP service is reachable by the attacker; no login is needed.
ProFTPD 1.3.5 (upstream) with mod_copy loaded, or a distribution package of it built before the 2015 fixes.
For command execution: the same host runs a web server that executes PHP from a folder the ProFTPD process can write to.
Copies run with the ProFTPD process's privileges, which limits which files can be read or written.
attack_path: Reconnaissance: attackers find internet-facing ProFTPD servers by their banner and version.
Initial access: unauthenticated copy commands move files on the server without logging in.
Data theft: sensitive files readable by the service are copied into a location the attacker can download from.
Execution: on hosts with a PHP-capable web server, attacker-controlled content is copied into the web folder and then requested over HTTP, running commands as the web server user.
Follow-on: from a web shell attackers can install tools, persist and move laterally; the sources read do not describe specific campaigns.
who_is_exposed: Any host running ProFTPD 1.3.5 with mod_copy enabled that was never updated, typically legacy Linux servers, hosting panels and appliances from 2014 to 2016.
Combined FTP and web servers (shared hosting, LAMP stacks) are at highest risk because the flaw becomes code execution.
Red Hat EPEL 5 and 6 shipped an older ProFTPD without mod_copy and are not affected (Red Hat Bugzilla).
detect: Version check: confirm the ProFTPD version and package release, and whether mod_copy is loaded, against the fixed versions below.
FTP logs: look for site copy commands issued before a successful login, or from unknown addresses.
File integrity: new or changed files in web folders, especially script files owned by the FTP service user.
Web server logs: first requests to newly created script files, followed by unusual child processes of the web server.
Network scanners: Tenable Nessus and SAINT both have checks for the mod_copy flaw.

steps: Find every host running ProFTPD and record version, package release and whether mod_copy is loaded.
Upgrade to ProFTPD 1.3.5a or later, or install your distribution's patched package.
If you do not use the copy feature, disable mod_copy in the ProFTPD configuration.
Restrict the FTP port to the addresses that need it; ProFTPD 1.3.5 is long out of support, so plan to move to a current release or SFTP.
Make sure the FTP service account cannot write to web folders that execute scripts.
US federal agencies: follow CISA's BOD 26-04 guidance and forensics triage requirements named in the KEV entry.
fixed_versions: Debian wheezy 1.3.4a-5+deb7u3, jessie 1.3.5-1.1+deb8u1, stretch and sid 1.3.5-2
Fedora 22 proftpd-1.3.5-6.fc22, Fedora 21 proftpd-1.3.5-5.fc21, EPEL 7 proftpd-1.3.5-5.el7
verify: Confirm the installed version or package release is at or above the fixed version and that the service was restarted.
Rerun a vulnerability scanner check for the mod_copy flaw against the server.
Confirm from the loaded module list whether mod_copy is still enabled, and that unauthenticated sessions cannot use copy commands.
if_compromised: Isolate the host and preserve FTP, web server and system logs and a disk image.
Look for and remove planted files in web folders, but assume a web shell gave the attacker command execution.
Rotate credentials and keys stored on the host or readable by the FTP and web service accounts.
Rebuild the host from a known-good image with a patched ProFTPD, then restore data.
Report to your national CERT (US federal agencies to CISA).

CVE-2015-3306.caveats: ProFTPD's own bug tracker and documentation did not load; the vendor fix is taken from distribution advisories and Red Hat's tracker. CISA's catalog page was not read; the KEV listing comes from CyberView's copy of the catalog feed. CISA has not said who is exploiting it. No upstream workaround was read; disabling mod_copy is standard configuration, not an advisory instruction.

CVE-2015-5477.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild: ISC reported public proof-of-concept code on 1 Aug 2015 and Sucuri reported attacks crashing customers' DNS servers on 2 Aug 2015. CISA added it to KEV on 8 Oct 2026 (due 11 Oct 2026).
CVE-2015-5477.how_exploited: A denial-of-service flaw in how BIND's named handles TKEY queries (a record type used for key exchange). A single specially crafted DNS query trips an internal REQUIRE assertion and named exits. The vulnerable code runs before access control lists and other service restrictions are checked, so an unauthenticated remote attacker can stop any reachable recursive or authoritative BIND server, taking down name resolution and with it mail and web services that depend on it.
preconditions: The attacker can send a DNS query to the server; no authentication and no particular configuration are needed.
The server runs an affected BIND 9 release: 9.1.0 through 9.8.x, 9.9.0 through 9.9.7-P1, or 9.10.0 through 9.10.2-P2 (ISC), or a vendor build of those that has not been patched.
Both recursive resolvers and authoritative servers are affected; ACLs that restrict who may query do not protect the server (ISC).
attack_path: Reconnaissance: attackers can find public BIND 9 servers with mass internet scanning; Errata Security warned all public BIND 9 servers could be knocked out in about an hour.
Impact: a crafted TKEY query makes named fail an assertion and exit, ending DNS service until it is restarted.
Repetition: because one packet suffices, attackers can resend it each time the service comes back, keeping the server down.
Downstream effect: Sucuri noted that a DNS outage also makes email and web services that depend on the server unavailable. No data theft or code execution is reported for this flaw.
who_is_exposed: Any organisation running unpatched BIND 9 as an internet-facing authoritative server or open or internal resolver, including old Linux distributions such as RHEL 6 and 7 before the July 2015 errata.
Network appliances and operating systems that embed BIND, such as Juniper Junos releases listed in the CISA catalog references; check each vendor's bulletin.
Long-lived legacy servers and embedded systems never updated since 2015.
detect: Version check: query the installed BIND package or the named version and compare with ISC's fixed releases or your vendor's errata.
DNS query logs: with query logging enabled, look for TKEY-type queries from unexpected clients; Sucuri noted TKEY requests are rare in normal traffic.
System logs: named exiting with a REQUIRE assertion failure message, followed by unexpected service restarts or DNS outages.
Service monitoring: repeated DNS resolution failures or named process crashes, especially in short bursts.

steps: Inventory every system running BIND, including appliances and network operating systems that embed it.
Upgrade to the patched ISC release closest to your current version, or install your operating system vendor's patched bind package.
For appliances such as Juniper Junos, apply the vendor's fixed release from its own security bulletin.
If a system can no longer be patched (BIND 9.8 and older lines received no ISC fix), migrate it to a supported BIND release or another DNS server.
Monitor named for crashes and keep a supervisor that restarts it while patching is under way.
fixed_versions: ISC BIND 9.9.7-P2 and 9.10.2-P3 (ISC); any later supported release
verify: Confirm the installed BIND version or package release is at or above the fixed version for your platform.
Confirm named was restarted after the update (Red Hat's packages restart it automatically) and that the running process reports the new version.
Watch logs for further assertion failures over the following days.
if_compromised: Restart named and restore DNS service, then patch before re-exposing the server.
Preserve query logs and system logs from the crash period and note source addresses of TKEY queries.
Ask your upstream provider to filter the attack traffic if crashes continue before patching is complete.
Report sustained attacks on critical DNS to your national CERT, and to CISA if you are a US federal agency under BOD 26-04.

CVE-2015-5477.caveats: ISC's advisory was read from its current knowledge base page; the CISA catalog page and Juniper's bulletin did not load, so the KEV entry was taken from CyberView's copy of the catalog feed and Junos fixed releases are not listed here. CISA has not said who exploited it recently; the 2015 attacks were reported by Sucuri. ISC lists no workaround.

CVE-2016-3081.exploitation_status: Known exploited: CISA added it to KEV on 8 Oct 2026 (due 11 Oct). JPCERT/CC confirmed public exploit code on 28 Apr 2016, and Japan's National Police Agency reported scanning that appeared to target it.
CVE-2016-3081.how_exploited: A remote code execution flaw in Apache Struts 2 when Dynamic Method Invocation is enabled. The framework lets a request name the action method to call; in affected versions that method name was evaluated as an OGNL expression without enough checking. An unauthenticated attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request to any Struts action, and the server runs arbitrary code with the privileges of the application server process, giving full control of the web application and a foothold on the server.
preconditions: The attacker can send HTTP requests to a Struts 2 application; no login or user interaction is needed.
Struts 2.3.20 to 2.3.28 (except 2.3.20.3 and 2.3.24.3), including products that bundle those versions.
Dynamic Method Invocation is enabled; it has been off by default since Struts 2.3.15.2, so only applications that turned it on are vulnerable.
attack_path: Reconnaissance: attackers scan for Struts applications, typically by their action URL patterns; Japan's police agency reported such scanning in 2016.
Initial access and execution: one crafted request to a Struts action runs code as the application server account (JPCERT confirmed operating system commands ran).
Persistence: typical follow-on for Struts flaws is dropping a web shell or other tooling under the application server account; the sources read do not describe specific campaigns.
Next steps: theft of application data and credentials, and movement to internal systems reachable from the server.
who_is_exposed: Java web applications built on Struts 2.3.20 to 2.3.28 that enable Dynamic Method Invocation, often custom or legacy internal and public-facing apps.
Commercial products that embed Struts 2; the CVE record links Oracle and Huawei advisories for affected products, so check each vendor's bulletin.
Applications that have not been rebuilt since 2016 are the most likely to still carry vulnerable libraries.
detect: Inventory: search application archives and servers for Struts 2 core library versions in the affected range, and check configuration for Dynamic Method Invocation being enabled.
Web and proxy logs: requests to Struts actions carrying unusual method-prefixed parameters or expression syntax; SAINT and other scanner vendors publish checks for this flaw.
Host: the Java application server process starting shells or other unexpected child processes, and new files in the web application folders.
Network: outbound connections from the application server to unfamiliar hosts after suspicious requests.

steps: Find every application and product using Struts 2, including bundled copies, and note its version and whether Dynamic Method Invocation is on.
Upgrade Struts to 2.3.20.3, 2.3.24.3 or 2.3.28.1, or preferably a current supported Struts release, and redeploy; Apache expects no compatibility issues.
If you cannot upgrade at once, disable Dynamic Method Invocation, which Apache and JPCERT recommend.
For commercial products, apply the vendor's own fix from its bulletin.
Place exposed Struts applications behind a web application firewall with rules for this flaw while upgrading.
US federal agencies: follow CISA's BOD 26-04 guidance and forensics triage requirements named in the KEV entry.
workarounds: Disable Dynamic Method Invocation if the application does not need it (Apache, JPCERT).
Use a custom ActionMapper built from the patched Struts source code (Apache, JPCERT); test before deploying.
verify: Confirm the deployed application contains a fixed Struts core library, not only the build file.
Confirm Dynamic Method Invocation is disabled in the deployed configuration if you used the workaround.
Rescan the application with a vulnerability scanner check for S2-032.
if_compromised: Isolate the server and preserve web, application server and system logs and a disk image.
Hunt for web shells and other files written by the application server account, and for processes it started.
Rotate credentials the application uses (databases, service accounts, keys) and those stored on the server.
Rebuild the server and redeploy a patched application from a clean build.
Report to your national CERT (US federal agencies to CISA).

CVE-2016-3081.caveats: CISA's catalog page was not read; the KEV listing comes from CyberView's copy of the catalog feed, and CISA has not said who exploits it. JPCERT's 2016 report of attack traffic did not say whether attacks succeeded. The follow-on stages are typical of Struts attacks rather than described for this flaw in the sources read.

CVE-2021-3199.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild: listed as successfully exploited in joint advisory AA26-281A (8 Oct 2026) on actors enabled by China-based Integrity Technology Group; CISA added it to KEV on 8 Oct 2026. Fixed since 2021.
CVE-2021-3199.how_exploited: Path traversal (CWE-22) in the upload service of ONLYOFFICE Document Server before 5.6.3, reachable when JWT signing is in use. A parameter of the image upload feature is not checked for directory traversal, so a crafted upload is written outside the intended folder. Writing files to chosen locations on the server can lead to remote code execution as the Document Server service. The joint advisory records the impact as an unauthorised write; it does not describe what the actors did next with this flaw.
preconditions: The Document Server upload service is reachable by the attacker; many instances are internet-facing so that editors and integrated apps can reach them.
Document Server is older than 5.6.3 (the joint advisory lists 5.1.5 through 5.6.2).
JWT is enabled on the instance; the NVD and CISA descriptions limit the flaw to that configuration.
Whether a valid token or account is needed is disputed: NVD scores it as needing no privileges, one secondary analysis says the attacker must be authenticated.
attack_path: Initial access: the attacker sends a crafted image upload to an exposed Document Server and writes a file outside the upload folder.
Execution: the written file is used to run code on the server as the Document Server service (NVD, CISA).

Follow-on activity is not tied to this flaw by the joint advisory; elsewhere in the same campaign the actors used VPN software for persistence, password spraying and scripted theft of email and credentials (AA26-281A).
An unconfirmed secondary analysis reports web shells placed on ONLYOFFICE servers and theft of integration tokens and database credentials from configuration files.
who_is_exposed: Self-hosted ONLYOFFICE Document Server (Docs) older than 5.6.3 with JWT enabled, including instances bundled with or connected to file-sharing platforms such as Nextcloud.
Old appliances, containers and virtual images that were never upgraded since 2021; the fix is over five years old, so exposure is concentrated in forgotten or end-of-life deployments.
Organisations in sectors named by AA26-281A as targets, including government, critical manufacturing, healthcare and information technology.
detect: Inventory every Document Server instance (including those inside containers or bundled with other apps) and check its version; anything before 5.6.3 is vulnerable.

Review web server and Document Server logs for upload requests whose parameters contain directory traversal sequences; AA26-281A advises reviewing web application logs for traversal, command injection and enumeration attempts.
Look for unexpected files written outside the upload and cache folders, especially script files in web-served directories.
Watch for the Document Server service starting shells or unexpected child processes, and for unusual outbound connections from the server.
Compare against the indicators published with AA26-281A in STIX format on CISA's advisory page.

steps: Upgrade ONLYOFFICE Document Server to a current supported release; 5.6.3 is the first fixed version (vendor changelog, HKCERT).
If an instance cannot be upgraded at once, take it off the internet and allow only the addresses of the applications that use it.
Treat any instance older than 5.6.3 that was reachable from the internet as possibly compromised and check it before returning it to service.
Rotate the JWT secret shared between Document Server and connected applications after upgrading.
Replace end-of-life and unmanaged deployments, as AA26-281A advises for old software.
verify: Confirm the running Document Server version is 5.6.3 or later (preferably the current release) on every node and container.
Re-scan the instance with your vulnerability scanner after the upgrade.
Confirm the JWT secret was changed and connected applications still validate against the new one.
if_compromised: Isolate the server and preserve logs, disk and memory images before cleaning up.
Rebuild the server from a known-good image at a current version rather than removing files one by one.
Rotate the JWT secret, database credentials and any integration tokens or keys held in Document Server configuration, and check connected platforms for misuse.
Look for lateral movement from the server and report the incident; US federal agencies must follow BOD 26-04 forensic triage requirements.

CVE-2021-3199.caveats: ONLYOFFICE published no advisory beyond a one-line changelog entry, and no technical write-up of the 2026 exploitation was found; AA26-281A only lists the flaw as successfully exploited. Whether an attacker needs a valid token is disputed. Attribution of follow-on web shells to this flaw comes from a secondary source and is unconfirmed.

CVE-2023-22894.exploitation_status: Known exploited: CISA added it to KEV on 8 Oct 2026 (due 11 Oct). Detailed proofs of concept were given to Strapi by the reporter in 2023. No attacker named in the sources read.
CVE-2023-22894.how_exploited: An information disclosure flaw in Strapi's content API filtering. Query filters could be applied to private user columns, and by watching how API responses change an attacker infers their values one piece at a time, recovering email addresses, password hashes and password reset tokens of administrators and API users. Strapi's advisory says this works without authentication up to 4.7.1; a leaked reset token lets the attacker take over a Super Admin account, and chained with the email template injection flaw CVE-2023-22621 it gives code execution on the server.
preconditions: The Strapi API is reachable by the attacker.
Strapi from 3.2.1 up to but not including 4.8.0.
Per Strapi's GitHub advisory no authentication is needed; the original CVE text (and NVD) describes it as needing admin panel access, with the reach depending on that account's permissions.
For code execution: chaining with CVE-2023-22621 on versions up to 4.5.5.
attack_path: Reconnaissance: attackers locate internet-facing Strapi instances.
Credential access: repeated filtered requests against user records leak password hashes and reset tokens.
Privilege escalation: a leaked reset token is used to set a new password on a Super Admin account.
Execution: with admin access, an email template is altered so that server-side template code runs (CVE-2023-22621), giving code execution as the Strapi process.
Follow-on: the sources read do not describe what attackers did after access.
who_is_exposed: Self-hosted Strapi headless CMS deployments on versions 3.2.1 to before 4.8.0, including all of Strapi v3, which is end of life.
Sites that expose the Strapi API and admin panel to the internet are at highest risk.
detect: Version check: confirm the installed @strapi/strapi package version is 4.8.0 or later.

Request logs: Strapi's advisory says attempts appear in GET request parameters; look for many filtered requests referencing password or reset token fields, using the search pattern published in the GitHub advisory.
Admin activity: unexpected password resets or logins on administrator accounts, and new administrator accounts.
Email templates: review current templates and database backups for unexpected code inside template delimiters, and request logs for template edits (CVE-2023-22621 guidance).

steps: Inventory all Strapi instances and their versions, including old v3 deployments.
Upgrade to Strapi 4.8.0 or later (Strapi's stated minimum); move v3 sites to a supported release since v3 gets no patches.
Search request logs for filtered requests on private fields as the advisory describes; treat matches as an incident.
Restrict access to the admin panel and API to the networks that need it.
US federal agencies: follow CISA's BOD 26-04 guidance and forensics triage requirements named in the KEV entry.
verify: Confirm the deployed package version is 4.8.0 or later in every environment and the service has been restarted.
Rerun a vulnerability scanner or dependency audit and confirm the advisory no longer matches.
if_compromised: Isolate the server and preserve request logs, the database and backups.
Invalidate all password reset tokens and force password changes for all administrators and API users; notify affected users.
Inspect email templates and remove injected code; assume code execution if templates were changed.
Rotate secrets the Strapi process could read (database credentials, API tokens, JWT secrets), and rebuild from a clean, patched image.
Report to your national CERT (US federal agencies to CISA).

CVE-2023-22894.caveats: Sources disagree on whether authentication is needed: the CVE and NVD text says admin panel access is required, while Strapi's own GitHub advisory says unauthenticated attackers can exploit it through 4.7.1. CISA has not said who is exploiting it or since when. The CISA catalog page did not show the entry; KEV dates come from NVD. Strapi lists no workaround other than upgrading.

CVE-2023-25914.exploitation_status: Known exploited: CISA added it to KEV on 25 Nov 2026 (due 28 Nov, forensic triage required). No attacker named, ransomware use unknown. Synacktiv's technical advisory with a demonstration has been public since 31 Oct 2023.
CVE-2023-25914.how_exploited: A path traversal flaw in the XML interface of the Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration and building system manager, which the device's web application uses. A file-download function does not check the file name the user supplies, so a crafted request can step outside the intended folder. Synacktiv found that this works without authentication. Because the application runs as root, the attacker can download any file on the device, including the system password hash file. Cracking those hashes gives logins that, chained with CVE-2023-25915, lead to command execution as root.
preconditions: The attacker can reach the AK-SM 800A web or XML interface over the network. DIVD scanned the internet in 2023 and found devices to notify, so some are directly exposed.
Firmware older than 3.3.
Synacktiv reports that no authentication is needed. CVSS vectors from DIVD and NVD assume a low-privileged account, and that difference is unresolved.
No user interaction is needed.
attack_path: Reconnaissance: attackers find AK-SM 800A system managers by their web interface on the internet or on flat store and site networks.
Initial access: a crafted file-download request through the XML interface reads arbitrary files as root.
Credential access: the attacker downloads the device's password hash file and configuration, then cracks the hashes offline to get valid logins.
Execution: with those logins the attacker uses CVE-2023-25915 to run commands as root and take full control of the controller.

Impact: control of a system manager lets an attacker change refrigeration, HVAC and lighting setpoints and alarms. In food retail this can mean spoiled stock and safety problems. The sources read describe no specific campaign.
who_is_exposed: Operators of Danfoss AK-SM 800A series system managers on firmware older than 3.3. These are common in supermarkets, cold stores and commercial buildings.
Highest risk: units whose web interface is reachable from the internet for remote service, or reachable through a flat store network.
Service contractors and integrators who manage fleets of these controllers remotely.
detect: Version check: read the firmware version from each AK-SM 800A web interface or from Danfoss service tools. Anything below 3.3 is vulnerable.
Exposure check: confirm whether the controller's web interface can be reached from the internet. DIVD notified owners of exposed vulnerable units in 2023, so check for such a notice.
Network and firewall logs: look for requests to the controller's web interface from unknown or internet addresses, and for unusually large responses that suggest file downloads.
Device behaviour: unexpected logins, new or changed user accounts, configuration or setpoint changes, and alarm suppression in the controller's event and audit log.
OT monitoring: OT vulnerability scanners can flag the vulnerable firmware, and OT network monitoring can flag new or unusual connections to the controller.
No indicators of compromise were published in the sources read.

steps: List every AK-SM 800A system manager and record its firmware version and whether it can be reached from the internet or from untrusted networks.
If the device is exposed, preserve evidence first as CISA's forensic triage guidance describes: export logs and configuration and note any recent changes.
Install the latest Danfoss AK-SM 800A software, version 3.3 or later, as Danfoss and DIVD advise. Patch this together with CVE-2023-25915 and CVE-2023-25913.
Take the controller's web interface off the internet. Reach it only through a VPN or a secured remote-access service, with firewall rules that allow only known service addresses.
After patching, change every account password on the device, because password hashes may already have been read.
If the firmware cannot be updated, CISA says to stop using the product, or at least fully isolate it from untrusted networks until it can be updated.
fixed_versions: AK-SM 800A software 3.3 or later (per DIVD and Synacktiv; Danfoss advises installing the latest software)
verify: Confirm in the web interface that each unit reports firmware 3.3 or later.
From an external network, confirm that the controller's web interface is no longer reachable.
Rescan with an OT vulnerability scanner and confirm the finding is gone.
if_compromised: Disconnect the controller from external networks and keep local control of refrigeration and HVAC running. Check that setpoints and alarms are correct and that stored goods are safe.
Preserve the controller's logs, configuration exports and network captures before changing anything.
Reflash the firmware with the official Danfoss 3.3 or later image, restore a known-good configuration, and reset all user accounts and passwords.
Rotate any credentials that were stored on the device or reused elsewhere, for example in remote-access tools or email alarm settings.
Report to Danfoss and to your national CERT. US federal agencies must report to CISA under BOD 26-04.

CVE-2023-25914.caveats: Danfoss advisory DSA-2023-08-01 returned 403 and was not read, so this rests on CISA, DIVD and Synacktiv, which agree. CISA's product data marks versions up to and including 3.3 as affected, while DIVD and Synacktiv say 3.3 fixes it: confirm with Danfoss. Synacktiv says no login is needed, but the CVSS vector assumes one. Scores differ: CISA 8.8, DIVD 9.9. Who exploited it, and when, is unknown.

CVE-2023-25915.exploitation_status: Known exploited: CISA added it to KEV on 25 Nov 2026 (due 28 Nov, forensic triage required). No attacker named, ransomware use unknown. Synacktiv's technical advisory with a demonstration has been public since 31 Oct 2023.
CVE-2023-25915.how_exploited: An OS command injection, classed as improper input validation, in the XML interface of the Danfoss AK-SM 800A system manager. A certificate-loading function builds a shell command from a file name the user supplies without sanitising it, so a logged-in attacker can embed extra commands in that value. The commands run as root, which gives full control of the device. Synacktiv showed that the logins needed can be obtained without authentication by first using CVE-2023-25914 to download and crack the device's password hashes.
preconditions: The attacker can reach the AK-SM 800A web or XML interface over the network.
Firmware older than 3.3.
A valid user account on the device. Synacktiv describes it as authenticated RCE. Default, weak or reused passwords, or hashes stolen through CVE-2023-25914, meet this requirement.
No user interaction is needed.
attack_path: Reconnaissance: attackers find AK-SM 800A web interfaces exposed to the internet or to flat site networks.
Credential access: the attacker uses CVE-2023-25914 to read the password hash file without logging in and cracks it offline, or uses default or reused credentials.
Execution: a logged-in request to the certificate-loading function of the XML interface carries injected commands, which run as root.
Persistence and control: with root access the attacker can install tools or a remote shell, change accounts, and alter the controller's software.
Impact: changing refrigeration, HVAC or lighting control and suppressing alarms, or using the device as a foothold into the site network. The sources read describe no specific campaign.
who_is_exposed: Operators of Danfoss AK-SM 800A series system managers on firmware older than 3.3. These are used in supermarkets, cold storage and commercial buildings.
Highest risk: units whose web interface is reachable from the internet, or that still use default or shared service passwords.
Service providers and integrators who manage these controllers remotely across many sites.
detect: Version check: anything below firmware 3.3 is vulnerable.
Controller audit and event log: look for logins from unusual addresses or at unusual times, certificate upload or load activity nobody requested, and account or configuration changes.

Network monitoring: outbound connections from the controller to the internet, especially downloads or long-lived sessions. These controllers normally have little reason to start outbound connections apart from configured alarm and service links.
Firewall and remote-access logs: inbound access to the controller's web interface from unknown sources.
OT monitoring: OT vulnerability scanners can flag the vulnerable firmware, and OT network monitoring can flag unusual connections to or from the controller.
No indicators of compromise were published in the sources read.

steps: List every AK-SM 800A unit with its firmware version and network exposure.
For exposed units, preserve logs and configuration first, as CISA's forensic triage guidance describes.
Install the latest Danfoss AK-SM 800A software, version 3.3 or later. This fixes CVE-2023-25915 together with CVE-2023-25914 and CVE-2023-25913.
Remove direct internet access to the controller's web interface and allow remote service only through a VPN or a secured remote-access service.
Change every device password after patching and do not reuse them across sites.
Where the firmware cannot be updated, isolate the unit from untrusted networks or stop using it, as CISA requires of federal agencies when no mitigation is available.
fixed_versions: AK-SM 800A software 3.3 or later (per DIVD and Synacktiv; Danfoss advises installing the latest software)
verify: Confirm that each unit reports firmware 3.3 or later.
Confirm from outside that the web interface is not reachable from the internet.
Rescan with an OT vulnerability scanner and confirm the finding is gone.
if_compromised: Isolate the controller from external networks while keeping local control running. Check setpoints, alarms and product temperatures.
Preserve the logs, configuration and any network captures before changing anything.
Reflash with official Danfoss firmware 3.3 or later instead of trusting the running system, restore a verified configuration and reset all accounts.
Check neighbouring systems on the site network for lateral movement, and rotate any credentials the device held or shared.
Report to Danfoss and to your national CERT. US federal agencies must report to CISA under BOD 26-04.

CVE-2023-25915.caveats: Danfoss advisory DSA-2023-08-01 returned 403 and was not read, so this rests on CISA, DIVD and Synacktiv, which agree. CISA's product data marks versions up to and including 3.3 as affected, while DIVD and Synacktiv say 3.3 fixes it: confirm with Danfoss. CISA says only 'remote attacker', but Synacktiv and the CVSS vector require a login. Scores differ: CISA 8.8, DIVD 9.9. Who exploited it, and when, is unknown.

CVE-2024-10441.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild: on 29 Oct 2026 Synology said attackers exploit a December 2024 fix (SA-24:20) on outdated DSM for ransomware; C3RB3R is reported. In CISA KEV since 18 Nov 2026.
CVE-2024-10441.how_exploited: Improper encoding or escaping of output in DSM's system plugin daemon lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker run arbitrary code (CVSS 9.8). The attacker reaches the device over the network, abuses the flaw in the daemon's handling of input to execute code on the NAS, and gains control of the device and the data on it. Synology describes the vector only as unspecified; reported attacks then encrypt shared folders with C3RB3R ransomware.
preconditions: The DSM interface is reachable by the attacker, from the internet (port forwarding, DMZ, UPnP) or the local network; no login or user action is needed.
Attackers scan for exposed devices and check their DSM version before attacking, according to Kaspersky.
attack_path: Reconnaissance: scanning for internet-exposed Synology devices and reading their DSM version.
Initial access and execution: unauthenticated code execution through the system plugin daemon on unpatched DSM.
Persistence: Synology tells owners to look for scheduled tasks and administrator accounts they did not create.
Impact: C3RB3R walks user folders, encrypts files with a .L0CK3D extension and drops a ransom note in each folder; backups on the same device are also encrypted.
who_is_exposed: Synology NAS owners running DSM 7.2, 7.2.1 or 7.2.2 builds older than the fixed builds, especially with the management interface reachable from the internet.
BeeStation owners on BeeStation OS before 1.1-65374.
Devices on end-of-life or long-unpatched DSM builds, and unofficial DSM installations that do not receive updates.
detect: Check the full DSM build string (Control Panel, Update and Restore) against the fixed builds, including the last digit.
Run Synology Security Advisor and review its findings.
Review Task Scheduler for tasks you did not create and User and Group for administrator accounts you did not add (Synology's signs of intrusion).
Look for files with the .L0CK3D extension or read-me3.txt notes in shared folders.
Check router port forwarding, DMZ, UPnP and IPv6 rules and QuickConnect for paths that expose DSM to the internet.

steps: Block internet access to the DSM management interface before updating.
Update DSM to the fixed build or later for your branch, and update all packages in Package Center.
Enable automatic DSM updates.
Turn off QuickConnect and remove port forwarding, DMZ and UPnP rules you do not need.
Keep an off-device backup (Hyper Backup or Snapshot Replication to another system) and confirm backup tasks complete.
Enable two-factor authentication for administrator accounts.
workarounds: Block access to the DSM management web interface from the internet (Synology, as reported by BleepingComputer).
verify: Confirm the DSM build shown in Control Panel matches or exceeds the fixed build for your branch.
Confirm from outside your network that the DSM login page is no longer reachable.
Re-run Security Advisor and confirm no warnings remain.
if_compromised: Disconnect the NAS from all networks without powering it off.
Preserve encrypted files and ransom notes on an external drive for investigation, and contact Synology Support rather than cleaning up yourself.
Reset the device, reinstall DSM, and do not restore settings from a backup taken after infection.
Rotate passwords and revoke tokens for services used on the NAS before restoring data from a clean off-device backup.
Report the incident to your national CERT or police cyber unit.

CVE-2024-10441.caveats: Synology's statement names advisory SA-24:20, which covers three CVEs, and does not say which one is exploited; CISA's KEV entry names CVE-2024-10441. 360 links the attacks to two newer DSM flaws fixed in September 2026, which Synology has not confirmed, so updating to the latest DSM, not only the 2024 fix, is the safer course. The technical vector is not public in the vendor advisory.

CVE-2024-27834.exploitation_status: Known exploited: CISA added it to KEV on 4 Nov 2026 (due 18 Nov) without naming who. It was first used publicly at Pwn2Own Vancouver 2024; Apple's advisories do not say it was exploited in the wild.
CVE-2024-27834.how_exploited: A flaw in WebKit, the browser engine behind Safari and every iOS browser, that lets an attacker who already has arbitrary memory read and write inside the browser bypass Pointer Authentication, the arm64e protection that detects tampered pointers. It is not an entry point on its own: it is the step that turns a memory corruption bug into code execution. At Pwn2Own it was chained with a separate integer underflow bug, so that loading attacker-controlled web content gave remote code execution in the browser.
preconditions: The victim loads attacker-controlled web content in Safari or another WebKit-based browser or app.
The attacker also has a second flaw that gives arbitrary read and write in the browser process.
An Apple device running a release before the May 2024 updates, or Linux software using WebKitGTK or WPE WebKit before 2.44.2.
attack_path: Delivery: the victim is led to a malicious or compromised web page, or one is shown in an app's web view.
Memory corruption: a separate WebKit bug gives the attacker read and write access in the browser's memory.
Mitigation bypass: this flaw defeats Pointer Authentication so the corrupted memory can redirect execution.
Execution: code runs in the browser's sandboxed renderer; full device compromise would need further flaws, which the sources do not describe.
who_is_exposed: iPhone and iPad users on iOS or iPadOS before 17.5, or before 16.7.8 on older devices.
Macs on Safari before 17.5 (Monterey, Ventura) or macOS Sonoma before 14.5.
Apple TV on tvOS before 17.5 and Apple Watch on watchOS before 10.5.
Linux desktops and embedded devices with WebKitGTK or WPE WebKit before 2.44.2.
detect: Version check: use your mobile device management or asset inventory to list OS and Safari versions below the fixed releases.
Linux: check installed WebKitGTK and WPE WebKit package versions against 2.44.2 or your distribution's fixed package.
Crash reports: repeated WebKit content process crashes after visiting particular sites can indicate failed exploitation.
Browsing logs: web proxy or DNS records of devices that visited suspicious sites before the device was updated.
No indicators or detection rules for in-the-wild use were published in the sources read.

steps: Update every Apple device to the fixed release or later (list below); current releases include the fix.
On Macs that stay on Monterey or Ventura, install Safari 17.5 or later through Software Update.
Update WebKitGTK and WPE WebKit on Linux to 2.44.2 or your distribution's fixed package.
Use device management to enforce minimum OS versions and block access from devices that are behind.
Retire devices that cannot run a fixed release.
US federal agencies: follow BOD 26-04 as named in the KEV entry.
fixed_versions: iOS 17.5 and iPadOS 17.5; iOS 16.7.8 and iPadOS 16.7.8
macOS Sonoma 14.5; Safari 17.5 for macOS Monterey and Ventura
verify: Confirm in device management that every device reports the fixed OS release or later.
On Macs, confirm the Safari version shown in About Safari is 17.5 or later.
On Linux, confirm the installed WebKitGTK or WPE WebKit package version and restart affected applications.
if_compromised: Take the device off sensitive networks and preserve a sysdiagnose or full backup for analysis before wiping.
Update or restore the device to the latest release, and reset passwords and sessions used from it from a clean device.
For high-risk users, consider Lockdown Mode and seek specialist mobile forensics help.
Report to your national CERT (US federal agencies to CISA).

CVE-2024-27834.caveats: Apple's advisories and the WebKitGTK advisory agree on the flaw, but give no technical detail, and none says it was exploited in the wild; CISA has not said who used it or when. The Pwn2Own chain is reported by BleepingComputer. Detection and compromise steps are general practice for browser exploit chains, not from the advisories.
