CVE-2026-109618.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild: CISA added it to KEV on 26 Oct 2026; Check Point Research saw PHP2Shell used against unpatched Mobile Access portals from 30 Oct 2026. PoC material circulated after a leak (PHP Foundation).
CVE-2026-109618.how_exploited: Memory corruption in PHP's out-of-memory handling (Canada's Cyber Centre classes it as use after free, CWE-416). If a request hits PHP's memory limit at a particular moment, internal request data is left partly initialised and request cleanup later treats it as valid. On Apache with mod_php an unauthenticated request can trigger this before any application code runs, and the PHP Foundation says code execution was shown with default settings; on PHP-FPM it was confirmed through application code paths. The attacker gains code execution as the web server or PHP worker account.
preconditions: A PHP installation that serves web requests is reachable: mod_php, PHP-FPM, php-cgi, FrankenPHP or LiteSpeed; PHP rates mod_php the highest risk.
PHP 8.2 to 8.5 before 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, any PHP 8.1 or older without a vendor backport, or PHP 8.6.0 builds before RC4.
No authentication or user interaction is needed; on mod_php no particular application is needed.
PHP bundled in other products, such as the Check Point Mobile Access portal, is exposed in the same way until the product vendor ships a fix.
attack_path: Initial access: crafted unauthenticated web requests drive a PHP worker into the vulnerable out-of-memory path; Check Point saw hundreds of crashes in portal Apache and PHP workers during the first wave.
Execution: the corrupted request state lets the attacker run code as the portal's or web server's service account.
Privilege escalation: on Check Point gateways the attacker chained a separate Gaia flaw (CVE-2026-123039) to gain root.
Persistence: webshells placed in the portal's template directory, plus standalone implants that Check Point links to the PhiliKit family.
Follow-on: network scanning, SSH to a VMware ESXi host with a service account, and a wiper that destroyed files on some Israeli victims' systems.
who_is_exposed: Internet-facing websites and applications on any affected PHP branch, most of all Apache with mod_php.
Products, appliances and containers that bundle PHP, including Check Point Security Gateways with the Mobile Access portal until patched.
Systems on PHP 8.1 or older, which the PHP project no longer fixes; only distribution or LTS vendor backports protect them.
detect: Version inventory: list every PHP runtime, including PHP bundled in appliances and container images, and compare with the fixed releases.
Process telemetry: PHP or web server worker processes starting shells or download tools (CISA); CISA publishes a SIGMA rule for this in its SIGMA_Rules repository.
Web server and PHP logs: bursts of worker segmentation faults or memory-limit errors from unauthenticated requests, as Check Point saw.
File integrity: new PHP files in template or upload directories and unexpected session files in temporary directories; compare with Check Point Research's published indicators.
Network: outbound connections from web servers to unfamiliar hosts, and SSH from web servers to hypervisors or other internal systems.

steps: Inventory every system running PHP, including PHP inside third-party products, appliances and containers.
Update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, or your distribution's patched package, starting with internet-facing systems, and restart all workers.
For PHP 8.1 and older, use a vendor backport or the PHP security team's minimal source backports, or upgrade to a supported branch.
For appliances that bundle PHP, apply the product vendor's own fix.
If you cannot patch now, take the PHP systems offline or off the internet until patched (CISA, Canadian Cyber Centre); a web application firewall may help in the meantime (CISA).
Hunt for compromise on any system that was exposed before patching.
fixed_versions: PHP 8.6.0 RC4 includes the fix; earlier 8.6.0 builds are affected
workarounds: PHP says these reduce exposure but do not make an installation safe: remove the finite memory limit by setting memory_limit to -1 through admin-level configuration.
Set a low post_max_size (8M without uploads, 32M with) and keep upload_max_filesize below it.
Enforce request size, field count, multipart part, header count and nesting limits at the web server or proxy, including requests without a usable length.
Use a container or cgroup memory limit that kills only the worker; PHP warns not to use address-space or data rlimits, which can trigger the flaw.
verify: Confirm each runtime reports a fixed version or your vendor's patched package release.
Confirm every PHP worker, FPM pool and Apache process was restarted after the update.
Rescan containers and appliances to confirm no vulnerable PHP build remains in use.
if_compromised: Isolate the server, keeping memory, logs and disk images for investigation.
Look for webshells, implants and persistence beyond PHP, as attackers escalated to root on Check Point gateways.
Rotate credentials stored on or reachable from the server, including database, service and hypervisor accounts.
Rebuild from a known good image, patch before reconnecting, and check hypervisors and other systems reached from it.
Report to your national CERT (in Canada via My Cyber Portal) and to CISA if you are a US federal agency under BOD 26-04.

CVE-2026-109618.caveats: The vendor advisory describes the mechanism only in general terms. Check Point's report ties the attacks to PHP2Shell, which covers this flaw and CVE-2026-109619, without saying which one was used. Attribution of the Check Point campaign is uncertain (Check Point). Check Point's own fixed versions for its gateways are not listed here. A separate flaw, CVE-2026-115560, is not fixed by these releases.

CVE-2026-109619.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild: CISA added it to KEV on 26 Oct 2026; Check Point Research saw PHP2Shell used against unpatched Mobile Access portals from 30 Oct 2026. PoC material circulated after a leak (PHP Foundation).
CVE-2026-109619.how_exploited: A use after free (CWE-416) from stale request state in PHP. If a fatal error happens at the wrong point, internal state owned by one request survives after its memory has been freed, and a later request handled by the same worker can use that stale state before normal initialisation resets it. PHP confirmed the use after free and worker crashes, and the reporter showed code execution against a real application on Apache with mod_php. Confirmed paths go through session upload progress and, on PHP 8.5, fatal error backtraces. Success gives code execution as the web server or PHP worker account.
preconditions: A PHP installation that serves web requests is reachable: mod_php, PHP-FPM, php-cgi, FrankenPHP or LiteSpeed; PHP rates mod_php the highest risk.
PHP 8.2 to 8.5 before 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, any PHP 8.1 or older without a vendor backport, or PHP 8.6.0 builds before RC4.

The attacker can cause a fatal error at the right moment, for example through session upload progress (on by default unless disabled), fatal error backtraces on 8.5, per-request settings that emit diagnostics early, or reachable timeouts.
No authentication is needed; a later request must be served by the same worker process.
attack_path: Initial access: unauthenticated requests force a fatal error that leaves stale state in a worker, then further requests to the same worker reuse it.
Execution: the freed memory is reused to run code as the web server or portal service account.
Privilege escalation: on Check Point gateways the attacker chained a separate Gaia flaw (CVE-2026-123039) to gain root.
Persistence: webshells in the portal's template directory and standalone implants that Check Point links to the PhiliKit family.
Follow-on: network scanning, SSH to a VMware ESXi host and a wiper used against some Israeli victims.
who_is_exposed: Internet-facing websites and applications on any affected PHP branch, most of all Apache with mod_php.
Products, appliances and containers that bundle PHP, including Check Point Security Gateways with the Mobile Access portal until patched.
Systems on PHP 8.1 or older, which the PHP project no longer fixes; only distribution or LTS vendor backports protect them.
detect: Version inventory: list every PHP runtime, including PHP bundled in appliances and container images, and compare with the fixed releases.
Process telemetry: PHP or web server worker processes starting shells or download tools (CISA); CISA publishes a SIGMA rule for this in its SIGMA_Rules repository.
PHP and web server logs: bursts of fatal errors, timeouts or worker crashes tied to upload or session handling from unauthenticated clients.
File integrity: unexpected session files in temporary directories and new PHP files in template or upload directories; compare with Check Point Research's published indicators.
Network: outbound connections from web servers to unfamiliar hosts, and SSH from web servers to hypervisors or other internal systems.

steps: Inventory every system running PHP, including PHP inside third-party products, appliances and containers.
Update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, or your distribution's patched package, starting with internet-facing systems, and restart all workers.
For PHP 8.1 and older, use a vendor backport or the PHP security team's minimal source backports, or upgrade to a supported branch.
For appliances that bundle PHP, apply the product vendor's own fix.
If you cannot patch now, take the PHP systems offline or off the internet until patched (CISA, Canadian Cyber Centre), and apply PHP's workarounds as a stopgap.
Hunt for compromise on any system that was exposed before patching.
fixed_versions: PHP 8.6.0 RC4 includes the fix; earlier 8.6.0 builds are affected
workarounds: Set session.upload_progress.enabled to 0 in php.ini, the FPM pool or server configuration (not at runtime or in user ini files) and restart every worker; PHP says this blocks the confirmed session paths only.
On PHP 8.5, set fatal_error_backtraces to 0 and restart every worker; this blocks only the confirmed backtrace path.
Remove invalid or deprecated per-request settings that emit diagnostics before initialisation; hiding errors does not help.
Fix fatal errors and execution timeouts that attackers can reach, including in callbacks, upload and import processing, and cleanup.
verify: Confirm each runtime reports a fixed version or your vendor's patched package release.
Confirm every PHP worker, FPM pool and Apache process was restarted after the update.
Where workarounds are used, confirm the effective configuration shows session upload progress disabled for every pool and virtual host.
if_compromised: Isolate the server, keeping memory, logs and disk images for investigation.
Look for webshells, implants and persistence beyond PHP, as attackers escalated to root on Check Point gateways.
Rotate credentials stored on or reachable from the server, including database, service and hypervisor accounts.
Rebuild from a known good image, patch before reconnecting, and check hypervisors and other systems reached from it.
Report to your national CERT (in Canada via My Cyber Portal) and to CISA if you are a US federal agency under BOD 26-04.

CVE-2026-109619.caveats: PHP says there are no complete mitigations and its workarounds block only confirmed paths. Check Point's report ties the attacks to PHP2Shell, which covers this flaw and CVE-2026-109618, without saying which one was used; attribution is uncertain. A related lower-risk flaw, CVE-2026-115560, is not fixed by these releases but is blocked by disabling session upload progress.

CVE-2026-110447.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild: administrators reported web shells from 10 Sep 2026, Italy's CSIRT reported a compromised server, and CISA added it to KEV on 23 Oct 2026. No actor named; CERT Polska's ransomware claim is unconfirmed.
CVE-2026-110447.how_exploited: Unauthenticated OS command injection (CWE-78) in the proxy component of the richdocumentscode app, the Built-in CODE Server for Nextcloud. The app starts its local Collabora server through a PHP shell call, and a crafted request to the app's proxy script makes the server run an operating system command as the web server user. It is reachable only while the built-in CODE server is not running, for example after a restart, upgrade or crash, and disabling the app does not stop it. Attackers used it to write PHP web shells into the app folder and then read files the web server can read.
preconditions: The Nextcloud server is reachable by the attacker, usually from the internet; no login or user interaction is needed.
The richdocumentscode app (Built-in CODE Server) is installed in a version before 26.4.303, even if it is disabled.
The built-in CODE server process is not running at the time of the request, such as after a container restart, an upgrade or a crash.
attack_path: Initial access: an unauthenticated request to the app's proxy script injects an OS command that runs as the web server user.
Persistence: PHP web shells written into the richdocumentscode app folder; Italy's CSIRT saw three on one server. Upgrading the app does not remove them.
Discovery: the attacker searched for password-manager files, password databases and cryptocurrency wallet files (administrator's logs, via Rescana).
Collection: in a case reported by Italy's CSIRT, the Nextcloud configuration file holding database credentials and application secrets was taken; no lateral movement or admin access was seen.
who_is_exposed: Nextcloud servers with the Built-in CODE Server app (richdocumentscode) before 26.4.303 installed, enabled or not.
Nextcloud 29 and older, which cannot install a fixed release and must upgrade Nextcloud or remove the app.
Not affected: standalone Collabora Online servers, Collabora Docker images and packages, Nextcloud All-in-One, and Nextcloud Office using a separate Collabora server.
detect: Run the Nextcloud integrity check and look for unexpected PHP files, starting with the richdocumentscode app folder.
Review web server access logs back to at least 10 Sep 2026 for unusual requests to the built-in app's proxy script.
Watch for outbound connections from the Nextcloud server to public callback services, and for unexpected sudo-failure emails from the web server account.
Check the installed richdocumentscode version in the Nextcloud app list; anything below 26.4.303 is vulnerable.

steps: Update richdocumentscode to 26.4.303 or later, or remove the app; disabling it is not enough.
On Nextcloud 29 or older, upgrade Nextcloud to 30 or later before updating the app, or remove the app.
For production document editing, consider a separate Collabora Online server, which is not affected; the app store calls the built-in app for testing and non-production use.
Check every server that had a vulnerable version for web shells and unexpected PHP files; the update does not remove them.
fixed_versions: richdocumentscode (Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server) 26.4.303 and later; 26.4.402 and 26.4.502 also include the fix
workarounds: Collabora gives no workaround other than upgrading or removing the app.
verify: The Nextcloud app list shows richdocumentscode 26.4.303 or later, or the app is no longer installed.
The Nextcloud integrity check reports no unexpected files after the update. If 26.4.402 fails to start, administrators report rolling back to 26.4.303 works.
if_compromised: Isolate the server and preserve web server logs and the app folder before cleaning up.
Remove web shells and unexpected PHP files, or rebuild the server from a known good state.
From a trusted system, rotate database passwords, mailbox passwords, app passwords and application secrets in the Nextcloud configuration, and check for reuse elsewhere.
Treat every file readable by the web server account as potentially exposed, and report the incident to your national CERT.

CVE-2026-110447.caveats: Collabora's advisory does not itself report exploitation; that comes from CISA, national CERTs and administrators. Severity is CVSS 4.0 9.2 (Collabora) or 3.1 9.8 (NVD). The number of hit servers, whether September and October activity is one campaign, and CERT Polska's ransomware link are unconfirmed. No full indicator list has been published. Some forum detail comes from individual administrators.

CVE-2026-110936.exploitation_status: Known exploited: Siemens advisory SSA-580366 states active exploitation; Siemens warned on 19 Oct 2026 that the Romulus ClickFix campaign abuses it. CISA added it to KEV on 20 Oct 2026. No public exploit code reported.
CVE-2026-110936.how_exploited: A DLL search-order (side-loading) flaw in Siemens Software Center, a Windows tool for downloading and managing Siemens software. Versions before 4.0.9.8 load helper libraries from their own folder without checking them, so a library placed next to the program runs with the program's privileges. In the observed campaign attackers did not attack existing installations: they shipped a genuine, validly signed copy of the program together with their own malicious library. A ClickFix lure tricks the user into running a command, which installs this bundle through an installer package; the trusted signed program then loads the attacker's library, which gives the attackers remote control of the PC.
preconditions: Code or files can be placed in a folder the program searches for libraries (Siemens: an authenticated local attacker; in the campaign, the attacker's own installer creates that folder).
A Siemens Software Center build before 4.0.9.8; Siemens names 3.5.8.7, the latest at the time, as the carrier used.

In the ClickFix campaign, a user is persuaded to paste and run a command copied from a web page; machines that never had the software installed are still at risk because attackers bring their own copy.
attack_path: Lure: a fake verification page (some campaigns reached via malicious ChatGPT custom GPTs, per Huntress as reported) tells the user to copy and run a command.
Delivery: the command starts PowerShell, which fetches an installer package from a Romulus distribution server and runs it through Windows Installer.

Execution: the installer places the signed Siemens Software Center program and a malicious library in a folder under the user's local application data, then starts the program, which loads the library.
Persistence: Siemens advises checking for a Siemens Software Center entry in startup applications or scheduled tasks on machines where it was never installed.
Objective: a remote access trojan gives the attackers control; Forescout links the same Romulus platform to LegionLoader, which steals browser data.
who_is_exposed: Windows PCs with Siemens Software Center older than 4.0.9.8, typically engineering workstations using Siemens design and industrial software.
Any Windows user who can be talked into running a ClickFix command, whether or not Siemens software is installed, because the attackers bundle their own signed copy.
Defences that trust a file only because it is signed by Siemens are bypassed, since the program itself is genuine and unmodified.
detect: Process: the Siemens Software Center program launched by the Windows Installer (msiexec) from a folder under the user's local AppData Programs directory, an unusual place for it to run (Siemens).
Files: a folder named SM Software Provisioning Service under the user's local AppData Programs directory, and unsigned libraries beside the Siemens program.
Persistence: a Siemens Software Center entry in startup apps or Task Scheduler on a machine where it was never installed.
Command history and EDR: PowerShell started from the Run dialog or clipboard content that downloads and runs an installer package.
Network: block and search proxy and DNS logs for the delivery, control and installer-hosting addresses and domain Siemens published in its 19 Oct 2026 blog post.
Version check: inventory Siemens Software Center installs and confirm they report 4.0.9.8 or later.

steps: Update Siemens Software Center to 4.0.9.8 or later; existing installs update themselves the next time the program starts, so start it on every machine that has it, or deploy the new version from Siemens' download page.
Block the indicators Siemens published (addresses, domain and installer name) on proxies, DNS filters and EDR.
Hunt for the program running from user AppData folders and for the provisioning-service folder on all Windows machines, not only those with Siemens software.
Reduce ClickFix risk: tell users that no real verification asks them to paste commands into Run or PowerShell, and consider restricting the Run dialog and PowerShell for ordinary users.
Install Siemens software only from official Siemens channels.
fixed_versions: Siemens Software Center V4.0.9.8 or later (all earlier versions affected)
workarounds: Siemens gives no product workaround beyond updating; its general guidance is to protect network access to devices and follow its industrial security operational guidelines.
verify: Confirm every install reports version 4.0.9.8 or later after it has been started once.
Confirm no Siemens Software Center copy runs from user AppData folders and no unexpected startup entry or scheduled task for it remains.
Confirm the published indicators are blocked and produce no hits after the change.
if_compromised: Isolate the machine from the network and preserve memory, EDR telemetry and the installer and library files for analysis.
Stop the malicious process and remove the related startup entries and scheduled tasks; prefer rebuilding the machine from a known good image.
Reset passwords and sessions for accounts used on the machine, including browser-saved credentials, since loaders in this campaign steal browser data.
Check other machines for the same indicators and report the incident to your CERT or Siemens ProductCERT.

CVE-2026-110936.caveats: Siemens' advisory was read in full; its 19 Oct blog post and the Huntress and Forescout reports were not read directly, so campaign details come from news reports quoting them. Scores differ: CVSS 3.1 6.7, CVSS 4.0 8.4. One report says the Huntress and Forescout write-ups do not name Siemens Software Center. Siemens says no Siemens system or update channel was breached.

CVE-2026-111357.exploitation_status: Known exploited as a zero-day since early Oct 2026: Volexity saw actor UTA0576 chain it with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-118527 from 3 Oct. CISA's alert confirms exploitation; KEV added 30 Oct 2026 (due 2 Nov).
CVE-2026-111357.how_exploited: A missing-authentication flaw in a privileged function of Ivanti Connect Secure that lets code already running on the appliance as a low-privileged user raise itself to root. It is the last link of a three-flaw chain: the CVE-2026-104935 authentication bypass and code execution give an unauthenticated internet attacker commands as the web server's cgi-server account, CVE-2026-118527 lets them place content in a predictable location, and this flaw then runs their commands as root. Together the chain gives full control of the VPN appliance without any login.
preconditions: On its own: the attacker already runs code on the appliance as a local low-privileged account (CISA: local authenticated attacker).
In practice: chained with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-118527, which only need network access to the appliance's web interface, typically internet-facing.
Ivanti Connect Secure 22.8R2.5 and earlier, 25.1.1.2 and earlier, and (per CISA) 25.1.2.2 and earlier; Volexity's victim ran 22.8R2.4, then fully patched.
attack_path: Initial access: the CVE-2026-104935 authentication bypass and code execution from the internet give commands as the cgi-server account.
Staging: CVE-2026-118527 lets the attacker place content in a predictable location on the appliance.
Privilege escalation: this flaw runs that content as root, giving full control of the appliance.

Stealth: UTA0576 left no web shell or implant, re-ran the whole chain for each command, changed library code only in memory, restored altered configuration data and evaded Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool.

Follow-on: theft of stored LDAP domain credentials, Active Directory queries for Windows LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys, and password spraying, which Volexity judged preparation for lateral movement.
who_is_exposed: Organisations running Ivanti Connect Secure VPN appliances, physical, virtual or cloud-hosted, on the affected releases.
Customers who upgraded to 22.8R2.5 or 25.1.1.2 for the October fix are still exposed to this flaw and must upgrade again.
Directories and accounts reachable from the appliance, because stored domain credentials are the attackers' main target.
The 22.8 branch reaches end of life on 31 Jan 2027 (CISA).
detect: Do not rely on Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool alone: CISA and Volexity say this activity evades it; use network and memory forensics.
Web logs: unusually high volumes of requests to the login-related welcome page and requests carrying a custom header whose value does not match the requested path (Volexity).
Appliance file system: an unusual data directory that should not exist, per the Volexity report.
Directory: LDAP queries from the appliance's service account for LAPS passwords or BitLocker recovery keys, and password-spraying failures sourced from the VPN appliance.
Indicators and YARA rules: use those published by Volexity, plus Ivanti's and Rapid7's threat hunting guidance; check logs for gaps or tampering.

steps: Preserve memory and logs from the appliance first where feasible (as advised in reporting on the Volexity findings), then upgrade at once to a release fixing all three chained flaws.
Investigate for compromise after patching using network and memory forensics, Ivanti's and Rapid7's hunting guidance and Volexity's indicators.
Restrict the appliance's administrative interface to trusted management networks.
Rotate credentials the appliance stores or uses (LDAP and domain service accounts, local administrators), and check whether LAPS passwords or BitLocker keys may have been read.
Plan migration off the 22.8 branch before its end of life on 31 Jan 2027, following Ivanti's 25.x upgrade and migration guide.
fixed_versions: Ivanti Connect Secure 22.8R2.6 (22.8R2.5 and earlier affected), as reported from Ivanti's 29 Oct 2026 advisory update
Ivanti Connect Secure 25.1.1.3 (25.1.1.2 and earlier affected), as reported from Ivanti's 29 Oct 2026 advisory update
25.1.2.x through 25.1.2.2 listed affected by CISA; confirm the fixed 25.1 build in Ivanti's advisory
verify: Confirm the appliance reports 22.8R2.6, 25.1.1.3 or a later fixed build, not the October builds 22.8R2.5 or 25.1.1.2.
Confirm a forensic review (memory and network) found no sign of the chain, since the integrity checker cannot show this.
Confirm rotated credentials are in place and old ones are rejected.
if_compromised: Back up the configuration, factory reset the appliance and upgrade to the latest version; rebuild virtual or cloud instances (CISA).
Restore the configuration, then reset all domain, administrator and local account passwords (CISA).
Revoke and reissue certificates stored on the appliance and reset stored API keys and license server credentials (CISA).
Hunt the internal network for use of stolen credentials, LAPS passwords or BitLocker keys, and report to CISA or your national CERT.

CVE-2026-111357.caveats: Ivanti's advisory page did not render for an automated reader, so this rests on CISA's alert and KEV entry and on news reports of Ivanti's advisory and Volexity's research. Ivanti scores it 8.8, NVD 7.0. Fixed builds 22.8R2.6 and 25.1.1.3 come from press reports, and the fixed 25.1.2.x build is unconfirmed. Volexity confirmed one victim; motive unclear.

CVE-2026-111497.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild: CISA added it to KEV on 27 Oct 2026 and HKCERT says it is being exploited. ELLIO reported exploit traffic using a public proof of concept. Public exploit code appeared within hours of the 21 Oct fix.
CVE-2026-111497.how_exploited: Out-of-bounds write caused by an unchecked return value in the Brotli decoder (CWE-252). Per the Node.js advisory, an invalid block switch in malformed compressed input was reported as a temporary need for more input instead of a format error, so the streaming decoder kept appending input to a small fixed internal buffer and wrote past its end. An unauthenticated attacker who can get a crafted Brotli stream decompressed by a vulnerable application can crash the process, read process memory or, per Node.js and Imperva's demonstration, run code as that process.
preconditions: The application decompresses Brotli data the attacker controls: an inbound request body, or a response fetched from a server the attacker controls (Field Effect).

A vulnerable decoder is in use: Brotli 1.0.3 to 1.0.9, 1.1.0, or 1.2.0, or a product that bundles one (Node.js 22, 24, 26 before the October fixes, .NET, Bun, Python Brotli, brotlicffi, Envoy, Istio and others).
No authentication or user interaction is needed. Having the library installed is not exposure on its own; the decoder must actually process attacker-supplied input (Rapid7, via Help Net Security).
In Envoy and Istio exposure exists only when decompression is enabled; a bare Node.js HTTP server does not decompress request bodies automatically (Field Effect).
attack_path: Initial access: the attacker sends Brotli-compressed content to an internet-facing service, API, proxy or gateway that decompresses it, or lures a client service into fetching a compressed response from an attacker server.

Execution: the malformed stream corrupts decoder memory; outcomes range from a crash to memory disclosure to code execution as the service account. Imperva needed several attempts to get code execution on an official Node.js 24.22.0 arm64 image.

Follow-on: ELLIO saw in-the-wild traffic using a public exploit that opens a shell, from infrastructure it had earlier tied to scanning of VPN appliances, PHP flaws and Kubernetes. No later stages have been published.
who_is_exposed: Internet-facing Node.js services on 22.x, 24.x or 26.x before 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1 that decompress untrusted Brotli through node:zlib, and all end-of-life Node.js lines, which get no fix.
Envoy and Istio gateways and service meshes with Brotli decompression enabled.
.NET, PowerShell, Bun and Python applications that decode untrusted Brotli, including self-contained .NET apps and Python wheels that bundle their own decoder.
Container images and appliances built before 21 Oct 2026; HKCERT lists downstream advisories from Cisco, F5, Palo Alto Networks, Microsoft, VMware, Oracle, Citrix and others.
detect: Inventory every copy of Brotli, including the copies bundled in Node.js, Bun, .NET runtimes, Python wheels, proxies and container images; an operating system package update does not fix bundled copies.
Check runtime versions on running workloads, not only in lockfiles, against the fixed versions listed by each vendor.
Watch for unexplained crashes, segmentation faults or restarts in services that handle compressed traffic; repeated crashes can be failed exploit attempts.
Look for shells or unexpected child processes started by Node.js, .NET or proxy processes, and for unexpected outbound connections from them.
ELLIO named one source address seen sending exploit traffic (reported by Help Net Security); check edge logs for it, but treat it as a starting point only.

steps: Patch internet-facing services first: upgrade Node.js to 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1, and move off end-of-life Node.js lines, which will not be fixed.
Upgrade Brotli libraries and bindings to 1.0.10, 1.1.1 or 1.2.1 (Python Brotli 1.2.1, brotlicffi 1.2.1.0), and apply the .NET, PowerShell, Bun, Envoy and Istio updates.
Update lockfiles, rebuild applications and container images, redeploy and restart services so the patched code is actually loaded (Aikido via Help Net Security).
Apply appliance and product fixes from downstream vendor advisories listed by HKCERT (Cisco, F5, Palo Alto Networks, Microsoft, VMware, Oracle and others).
Because it is exploited, review internet-facing services that decompressed untrusted Brotli while vulnerable for signs of compromise.
workarounds: Neither Google nor Node.js gives a workaround. Where patching must wait, Field Effect suggests disabling Brotli decompression in Envoy and Istio on inbound or outbound paths after checking what depends on it.
verify: Running processes report the fixed runtime version (for Node.js, check the version reported by each running service, not the build host).
Rebuilt container images and deployed artifacts contain Brotli 1.0.10, 1.1.1, 1.2.1 or later, confirmed with a software bill of materials or dependency scan.
Downstream products show the build named as fixed in their vendor advisory.
if_compromised: Isolate the affected host or container and preserve crash dumps, logs and the running image before rebuilding.
Rebuild from a patched image rather than cleaning in place.
Rotate secrets and tokens the compromised process could read, such as environment variables, API keys and cloud credentials.
Report the incident to your national CERT; US federal agencies follow CISA's BOD 26-04 forensic triage requirements.

CVE-2026-111497.caveats: The GitHub advisory GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35 returned not found when read, so version ranges come from the release, Node.js, HKCERT and Field Effect. Field Effect, written before the KEV listing, did not report in-the-wild use; CISA and HKCERT now do. Code execution was shown to be unreliable. Severity differs: CVSS 4.0 9.2 from Google, High from Node.js, 8.1 from Microsoft for .NET. No victims or actors are named.

CVE-2026-111560.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild: Barracuda said on 9 Nov 2026 the chain with CVE-2026-116606 was used against a small number of organisations. In CISA KEV (federal deadline 13 Nov). Singapore's CSA reports public exploit code. No actor named.
CVE-2026-111560.how_exploited: OS command injection (CWE-78) in the timezone setting of several Barracuda appliances' administrative interface. Per Mandiant, the value is not cleaned of shell metacharacters, so an administrator can set a crafted timezone that later runs operating-system commands as root. On its own it needs admin access, but on the Email Security Gateway it is chained with CVE-2026-116606, a pre-authentication authorisation bypass in the Admin UI, so an unauthenticated attacker who can reach that interface can gain root on the device.
preconditions: The attacker can reach the appliance's administrative interface (web Admin UI); Barracuda says devices whose admin interface is not reachable from the internet are less exposed.
Administrative access is needed for this flaw alone; on ESG, CVE-2026-116606 removes that requirement for anyone who can reach the Admin UI.
The device runs an unpatched release, per Mandiant ESG 9.4.0.27 and earlier, ADC 6.4.0, WAF 11.0.1, WSG 16.1.100.100, BMA 5.5.4.0, WCC 2.2.1 and earlier.
attack_path: Initial access: on ESG, the attacker uses CVE-2026-116606 to bypass Admin UI authorisation (SecurityWeek reports it abuses backup restore to change the configuration); on other products, stolen or weak admin credentials would be needed.
Execution: a crafted timezone value is saved through the admin interface and later processed by the system, running commands as root.
Impact: root control of the appliance, which sits in the mail or web traffic path. Barracuda and CISA have not published what attackers did after gaining access.
Scanning: Previdian reported 17 attempts against CVE-2026-116606 from 15 IP addresses between 9 and 11 Nov 2026 (as reported by SecurityWeek).
who_is_exposed: Barracuda Email Security Gateway appliances, most at risk because the pre-authentication bypass chains with this flaw.
Barracuda Load Balancer ADC, Web Application Firewall, Web Security Gateway, Message Archiver and WAF Control Center, where an attacker needs admin access.
Any affected device whose Admin UI is reachable from the internet or from untrusted networks, or that has not applied the November 2026 patches.
detect: Confirm each device shows the latest firmware and that the product's patch (BNSF, BNADC, BNMA, BNWF or BNYF number) is applied; a device without it should be treated as possibly exposed since early November 2026.
Review Admin UI access logs for logins or configuration changes from unexpected addresses, especially from the internet, and for backup restores nobody scheduled.
Look for unexpected changes to the system timezone setting or other configuration in the appliance's audit or change history.
Barracuda publishes no indicators of compromise; contact Barracuda Support if compromise is suspected.

steps: Apply the vendor patch now, or confirm automatic patching has applied it: ESG BNSF-40425 (9.4.017 and later) or BNSF-40430 (earlier); ADC and WAF BNADC-16586; BMA BNMA-32468; WCC BNWF-60060; WSG BNYF-24789.
Devices several versions behind may need multiple updates; follow the manual steps on Barracuda Campus linked from the advisory.
Restrict the administrative interface to trusted internal networks with network access controls.
Enable automatic patching, as Barracuda recommends.
Because exploitation is confirmed, check for compromise before and after patching (CISA BOD 26-04 asks federal agencies for forensic triage).
fixed_versions: Load Balancer ADC and Web Application Firewall: BNADC-16586
workarounds: Restrict access to administrative interfaces to trusted internal networks and limit exposure with network access controls (Barracuda; also Singapore's CSA).
verify: The device shows the latest firmware version available and the patch for its product is listed as applied.
The Admin UI is no longer reachable from the internet or untrusted networks.
if_compromised: Contact Barracuda Support, which the advisory names for suspected compromise.
Isolate the appliance from management networks and preserve its logs and configuration before changes.
Rotate admin passwords and any credentials stored on the device (directory, mail relay, certificates and keys).
Review mail or web traffic that passed through the device and connected systems for follow-on access; report to your national CERT.

CVE-2026-111560.caveats: Barracuda and CISA have not described the attacks or what attackers did after gaining root. Severity scores differ: Barracuda and Mandiant give 8.6, Singapore's CSA gives 7.2. Singapore's CSA says public exploit code exists; SecurityWeek does not mention it. Mandiant lists affected versions but no fixed versions; fixes here are Barracuda's patch identifiers.

CVE-2026-111793.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild: the developer told JPCERT/CC that attacks have been observed (JVN, 9 Nov 2026). Attackers, targets and dates are not named. In CISA KEV since 10 Nov 2026, federal due date 24 Nov.
CVE-2026-111793.how_exploited: Incorrect resource transfer between spheres (CWE-669) in Webtop Media Transcoder, the component that converts webmail attachments for viewing. It does not enforce the file-type restrictions an administrator sets. A signed-in user who goes around the Webmail interface and submits a specially crafted file directly to the transcoder can have blocked document types processed and converted, and JVN says this can expose sensitive information.
preconditions: The attacker has a valid Webtop webmail account (authenticated).
The attacker can reach the Media Transcoder service directly rather than only through the Webmail interface.
Webtop Media Transcoder older than version 1.1.22.0.
attack_path: Initial access: the attacker signs in with a valid account, either their own or a stolen one.
Execution: they bypass the Webmail interface and submit a crafted file of a blocked type to the transcoder.
Impact: the transcoder converts it anyway, and the attacker obtains information the restriction was meant to protect; neither the vendor nor JVN describes what attackers did next.
who_is_exposed: Organisations running Openwave Webtop webmail with a Media Transcoder older than 1.1.22.0.
Deployments where the transcoder can be reached by users other than through the Webmail front end are most at risk.
detect: Check the installed Media Transcoder version; anything below 1.1.22.0 is affected.
Review transcoder logs for conversion requests of file types the administrator has blocked, and for requests that did not come through the Webmail front end.
Look for unusual volumes of conversion requests from a single account or address.
Neither the vendor nor JVN has published indicators of compromise or detection rules.

steps: Upgrade to the latest supported Media Server 2.0 release, as the vendor recommends; the fix has been present since Media Transcoder 1.1.22.0.
Contact Openwave for patch details if you run an older branch, as JVN advises.
Until upgraded, make sure the transcoder only accepts requests from the Webmail servers, not directly from users or the internet.
US federal agencies: meet the 24 Nov 2026 KEV deadline and BOD 26-04 forensics triage requirements.
fixed_versions: Webtop Media Transcoder 1.1.22.0 and later (released 6 Dec 2021)
Vendor recommends the latest supported Media Server 2.0 release
verify: Confirm the transcoder reports version 1.1.22.0 or later, or the current Media Server 2.0 release.
Confirm that a blocked file type is refused when submitted through any path to the transcoder.
if_compromised: Preserve transcoder and webmail logs covering the suspicious requests.
Identify the accounts used, reset their passwords and end their sessions.
Work out which documents or data the conversions exposed and notify affected users as required.
Report the incident to Openwave and your national CERT.

CVE-2026-111793.caveats: Sources are thin. The vendor advisory does not say what kind of information is exposed and only says the bypass works mainly when the Webmail interface is bypassed; the restriction-bypass-only description differs from JVN's critical rating. The fix dates from 2021 but was disclosed in October 2026, with no explanation. The network-isolation step is a general hardening measure, not a vendor workaround.

CVE-2026-112967.exploitation_status: No exploitation reported. Microsoft (10 Nov 2026) marks it not exploited, not publicly disclosed and 'Exploitation Less Likely'; not in CISA's KEV catalog. CrowdStrike reports no exploitation.
CVE-2026-112967.how_exploited: A heap-based buffer overflow in the Windows Xbox Live Networking Service. Microsoft says an attacker on the same network, without any credentials, can call the service's endpoints in a way that overflows a heap buffer and runs the attacker's code on the Windows machine through that service. No user interaction is needed.
preconditions: The attacker is on a network that can reach the target machine (Microsoft: an in-network attacker); no authentication or user interaction (CVSS AV:N/PR:N/UI:N).
The Xbox Live Networking Service is present and running on the machine; CrowdStrike says exposure depends on this.
Windows 10 (1809, 21H2, 22H2) or Windows 11 (23H2 to 26H2) without the November 10, 2026 update; Microsoft lists no Windows Server release.
attack_path: Initial access: an attacker on the local or corporate network reaches the service on a Windows 10 or 11 machine.
Execution: crafted calls to the service's endpoints trigger the heap overflow and run code through the service.
Follow-on (no attacks seen): an attacker would be expected to use the foothold to steal credentials and move to other machines on the same network.
who_is_exposed: Windows 10 and Windows 11 machines on the listed releases where the Xbox Live Networking Service runs.
Consumer editions and gaming-enabled configurations are the main population; CrowdStrike rates it lower priority for most corporate fleets.
Machines on shared or untrusted networks (home, guest Wi-Fi, flat corporate networks) where other devices can reach them.
detect: Version check: confirm Windows 10 and 11 machines run at least the fixed November 2026 build for their release.
Inventory: find machines where the Xbox Live Networking Service is installed and running, since only those are exposed.
Event logs: crashes or unexpected restarts of the Xbox Live Networking Service.
Endpoint telemetry: unexpected child processes or outbound connections from the service host process for that service.
No indicators of compromise or detection rules have been published for this flaw as of 19 Nov 2026.

steps: Install the November 10, 2026 Windows cumulative update on all Windows 10 and Windows 11 machines in your normal cycle; there is no separate fix.
Bring forward machines where the Xbox Live Networking Service runs, particularly those on shared or untrusted networks.
On corporate machines that do not need Xbox features, review whether the service is needed, following your own build standards; Microsoft lists no workaround.
Use host firewalls to limit which devices on the network can reach workstations.
verify: Confirm each machine reports a build at or above the fixed build for its release (winver or update history).
Confirm patch compliance reports cover home and remote machines, not only those on the office network.
if_compromised: Isolate the machine from the network and preserve memory and event logs.
Reset passwords for accounts that signed in on the machine.
Reimage the machine from known-good media and install current updates before reconnecting.
Check other machines on the same network segment for similar activity.

CVE-2026-112967.caveats: Only Microsoft's one-sentence FAQ describes the attack; no researcher write-up exists. Microsoft does not say which endpoints or ports are involved or whether the service runs by default on enterprise editions. Some trackers list an Xbox flaw under CVE-2026-66801 instead; Microsoft's record confirms this id. Priority reflects no exploitation and limited corporate exposure.

CVE-2026-114625.exploitation_status: Known exploited: Arista said on 22 Oct 2026 it is actively exploited; CISA added it to KEV on 23 Oct 2026 (due 26 Oct) with forensic triage required. No attacker has been named.
CVE-2026-114625.how_exploited: A SQL injection flaw (CWE-89) in the web interface of on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO), the management portal for VeloCloud SD-WAN. An attacker who already holds a valid portal session, even with the lowest built-in tenant role, sends crafted input that the orchestrator passes into a database query. That lets them gain operator privileges and act as the local superuser operator, reaching functions meant only for internal use. With that control they can read and change the orchestrator's configuration and the SD-WAN data it manages and affect the VCO host itself (Arista, CISA).
preconditions: Network access to the VCO web interface; Arista notes VCO is exposed by default and no setting prevents that.
A valid authenticated session with at least the Enterprise Read Only role, so any stale, shared, partner or stolen low-privilege account is enough.
No user interaction is needed.
On-premises VCO 5.2 before 5.2.3.18, 6.1 before 6.1.3.10, or 6.4 before 6.4.2.12; Arista-hosted and dedicated instances were already patched.
attack_path: Initial access: the attacker logs in to the VCO portal with any valid account, including a read-only tenant account.
Privilege escalation: crafted input to the web interface is injected into a database query, giving operator rights as the local superuser operator.
Execution and impact: with internal functions exposed, the attacker can change orchestrator settings and SD-WAN data and impact the VCO host (Arista, CISA).

Persistence and follow-on: Arista tells customers to look for backdoor daemons, webshells, unexpected outbound connections and unexplained administrator changes, which suggests the activity it expects; it has not published what the attackers did.
who_is_exposed: Organisations running on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator on the affected release trains, especially where the portal is reachable from the internet.
Managed SD-WAN providers and enterprises with many tenant, partner or read-only accounts on the portal.
Releases fixed for the earlier exploited VCO flaws CVE-2026-16812 and CVE-2026-93952 are still exposed to this one (SOCRadar).
Not affected per Arista: VeloCloud Gateway and Edge, EOS switches and CloudVision; end-of-support VCO releases were not assessed.
detect: Version check: confirm every on-premises VCO runs 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10, 6.4.2.12 or later in its train.
VCO web access logs: look for unusual URL-like path components, encoded characters, references to local or internal services and bursts of requests, as Arista's advisory lists.
Block and search logs for the two attacking source addresses published in Arista Security Advisory 0199 (see the advisory for the values).
Audit recent administrator and operator activity in VCO for changes nobody made, and for low-privilege accounts acting with operator rights.
On the VCO host: look for unknown listening daemons, webshells in the web application folders and unexpected outbound connections.

steps: Before changing anything on a VCO that may be compromised, preserve web access, application, system and database logs and file-system timestamps, as Arista advises (CISA requires forensic triage for this entry).
Upgrade on-premises VCO to 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 or 6.4.2.12 or a later release in the same train; customers on unsupported trains should contact Arista TAC for an upgrade path.
Restrict the VCO web interface to trusted administrative networks.
Review portal accounts: disable stale, shared and unused partner accounts and reset credentials that may have been exposed.
Block the attacking addresses Arista published and limit outbound ports from the VCO host to what it needs.
fixed_versions: VCO 5.2.3.18 and later in the 5.2 train
VCO 6.1.3.10 and later in the 6.1 train
VCO 6.4.2.12 and later in the 6.4 train
workarounds: Arista gives no full workaround; until patched, restrict web interface access to trusted administrative networks, monitor for connections from the published malicious addresses and watch for unexpected outbound traffic from the VCO host.
verify: Confirm the running VCO version in the product itself, not from the date of the last update.
Confirm the web interface is no longer reachable from untrusted networks.
Re-check web access logs after the upgrade for continued attempts from the published addresses.
if_compromised: Isolate the VCO from untrusted networks while keeping evidence: preserve logs, database and file-system timestamps before rebuilding.
Contact Arista TAC for incident support.
Look for and remove backdoor daemons and webshells, or rebuild the orchestrator from a known-good release and restore checked configuration.
Rotate all VCO portal and operator credentials and any secrets the orchestrator holds, and review SD-WAN configuration pushed to Edges for unauthorised changes.
Report the incident to your national CERT; US federal agencies follow CISA's BOD 26-04 forensic triage requirements.

CVE-2026-114625.caveats: Arista has not named the attackers or described what they did after gaining operator rights, so the attack path beyond privilege escalation is inferred from the advisory's hunting advice. The two published attacking addresses may change. Reports differ on whether earlier VCO fixes help: they do not cover this flaw.

CVE-2026-114713.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild: the UnrealIRCd maintainer said attackers are exploiting it on the internet, with attempts reported from 8 Nov 2026; CISA added it to KEV on 13 Nov 2026 (deadline 16 Nov). No attacker named.
CVE-2026-114713.how_exploited: An escaping bug (improper neutralisation of delimiters) in UnrealIRCd's handling of the IRCv3 label message tag. Any ordinary connected user can put line breaks into the tag, which the server then relays unescaped into server-to-server traffic; the linked server reads the injected text as separate commands carrying server authority. The maintainer says this lets any user KILL other users, set network-wide bans (GLINE) and do much more, in practice IRC operator-level control of the network.
preconditions: The network links two or more UnrealIRCd servers, since the injection rides on server-to-server traffic.
A server runs UnrealIRCd 6.0.0 to 6.2.7 without the 7 Nov hot patch, or UnrealIRCd 5 (end of life) without the module blocked.
The attacker only needs to connect as an ordinary user; no operator account is required.
attack_path: Initial access: the attacker connects to a public IRC server as a normal user.
Execution: messages carrying a malformed label tag cause commands to be injected into the link to other servers, where they run with server authority.
Impact: the attacker can disconnect users, ban users or servers network-wide and take other operator actions; the maintainer has not described what attackers did after exploiting it.
who_is_exposed: Operators of IRC networks with two or more linked UnrealIRCd 6 servers before 6.2.7.1.
UnrealIRCd 5 networks (end of life since 1 July 2023), which are also affected; older 3.2.x and 4 releases were not checked.
Windows servers, which cannot be hot-patched and need the workaround and an upgrade.
detect: List the running version of the labeled-response module on each server as an IRC operator: a hot-patch version string or 6.2.7.1 means fixed; plain 5.0 with no patch suffix means unpatched (maintainer's advisory).
Review server logs and operator notices for KILL, GLINE and other operator actions that no operator issued, especially ones attributed to a server rather than a person.
Look for client messages carrying unusually long or malformed label tags in logs or spamfilter hits once the workaround is in place.
No indicators of compromise or detection rules have been published by the maintainer or CISA.

steps: First, have an IRC operator add the spamfilter workaround from the maintainer's advisory; it protects the whole network only if every linked server runs 6.0.4 or newer.
Then hot-patch every server running 6.0.0 to 6.2.7 with the bundle dated 7 Nov 2026 (no restart; not available on Windows), or upgrade to 6.2.7.1 and restart.
UnrealIRCd 5: block the labeled-response module in the configuration on all servers and do a full restart, not a rehash; plan a move to version 6.
Windows: apply the workaround immediately, then download and install 6.2.7.1.
Federal civilian agencies: the KEV deadline was 16 Nov 2026.
fixed_versions: UnrealIRCd 6.0.0 to 6.2.7 with the hot-patch bundle of 7 Nov 2026 applied
workarounds: An operator-applied spamfilter rule that blocks the malformed label pattern, given in the maintainer's advisory; effective only when every linked server runs 6.0.4 or newer, and it does not fix the eight other issues in 6.2.7.1.
UnrealIRCd 5: blacklist the labeled-response module and restart.
verify: Check that the hot-patch run ended with the success message saying all should be good; a rerun that says the patch is already applied does not prove it is running (UnrealIRCd FAQ).
List loaded modules on every linked server, including remote ones, and confirm the labeled-response module shows the hot-patch version or 6.2.7.1.
if_compromised: Review and remove bans, operator changes and configuration changes made by injected commands, and check for unknown linked servers or operator accounts.
Change operator and server link passwords if there is any sign they were used or exposed.
Keep server logs for the period since 7 Nov 2026 and report abuse to your national CERT where users or infrastructure were harmed.

CVE-2026-114713.caveats: The maintainer's forum advisory blocked automated reading; its content was read through the maintainer's identical oss-security post, and the exploitation quote through The Hacker News. Attacker identity, goals and actions after exploitation are not public. The CVSS score is 8.6 in reporting and 7.7 on file; the maintainer calls it critical.

CVE-2026-114819.exploitation_status: Public research: Depthfirst on 18 Nov 2026 described a no-login chain with CVE-2026-91609. No exploitation in the wild reported (CISA ADP: none). Fixed in Oracle's November 2026 update, published 17 Nov.
CVE-2026-114819.how_exploited: Flaw in the Oracle Text component of Oracle Database Server, rated 9.9 by Oracle with a scope change. On its own, Oracle's record says a low-privileged attacker with only the right to open a session can exploit it over Oracle Net and take over Oracle Text, with effects on other products. Depthfirst describes it as memory corruption in engine code and reports chaining it with CVE-2026-91609, a flaw in Oracle's GraphQL interface fixed in October, so that an attacker with no credentials, reaching an exposed HTTP endpoint, runs commands as the database's operating-system service user.
preconditions: Oracle Database Server 19.3 to 19.32, 21.3 to 21.24, or 23.4.0 to 23.26.3 without the November 2026 update.
Alone: a database account with the right to create a session and network access over Oracle Net (Oracle CNA record).

In the chain Depthfirst describes: no account, but an exposed HTTP endpoint backed by an Oracle REST Data Services or GraphQL interface vulnerable to CVE-2026-91609 (affected 24.2.0 to 26.2.1 per The Hacker News).
attack_path: Initial access (chain): the attacker reaches an internet-facing REST or GraphQL endpoint in front of the database and abuses CVE-2026-91609 before any login, so database roles do not stop it (Depthfirst).
Initial access (alone): the attacker logs in with any account that can open a session.
Execution: the Oracle Text flaw corrupts memory in the database engine and gives command execution as the database's operating-system service user (Depthfirst).
Impact: full control of the database and of other products sharing the host; no post-exploitation activity has been reported.
who_is_exposed: On-premises and self-managed cloud Oracle Database 19c, 21c and 23 deployments in the affected ranges, especially those with Oracle Text in use or installed.
Databases fronted by Oracle REST Data Services or a GraphQL interface reachable from the internet, which Depthfirst's no-login chain needs.
Any database where many users or applications hold accounts able to open a session, for the authenticated route.
detect: Check each database's release update level against Oracle's November 2026 patch for 19c, 21c and 23, and each Oracle REST Data Services install against 24.2.0 to 26.2.1.
Review Oracle REST Data Services and web-server access logs for unusual GraphQL or REST requests from unknown sources, especially failures followed by database errors.
Watch the database alert log and trace files for internal errors or process crashes in Oracle Text activity.
Look for shells or other unexpected child processes started by the oracle operating-system account, and for new files it writes outside normal directories.
Neither Oracle's record nor Depthfirst publishes indicators or detection rules for this flaw.

steps: Apply Oracle's November 2026 security patch for Oracle Database 19c, 21c or 23 to every affected database, following Oracle's own patch notes for the exact patch for your release.
Apply Oracle's October 2026 update for Oracle REST Data Services (CVE-2026-91609), which closes the no-login route in the chain.
Until patched, remove internet access to Oracle REST Data Services and GraphQL endpoints that do not need to be public, and restrict Oracle Net listeners to known application hosts.
Review accounts holding the right to create sessions; remove unused accounts and rotate widely shared credentials.
If Oracle Text is not used, consult Oracle's guidance on whether it can be removed; do not remove it without vendor guidance.
fixed_versions: Oracle Database Server 19c, 21c and 23 with the November 2026 security patch (exact patch levels in Oracle's bulletin)
verify: Confirm in the database's patch inventory that the November 2026 patch for its release is installed on every instance and every node of a cluster.
Confirm the Oracle REST Data Services version is outside 24.2.0 to 26.2.1.
Confirm from outside your network that REST and GraphQL endpoints you closed are no longer reachable.
if_compromised: Isolate the database host and the REST or GraphQL front end; preserve the alert log, trace files, web access logs and operating-system logs.
Rotate all database account passwords, wallet and key-store secrets, and credentials readable by the oracle operating-system account.
Rebuild compromised hosts from clean images on patched releases and restore data from a backup taken before the suspected compromise.
Review connected systems and database links the attacker could reach, and report the incident to your national CERT or incident-response provider.

CVE-2026-114819.caveats: Oracle's November 2026 bulletin refused automated reading (403), so this analysis uses Oracle's own CVE record, Depthfirst and The Hacker News; exact patch numbers are not given here. Oracle's record describes an authenticated flaw, while the no-login route relies on chaining with CVE-2026-91609 as reported by the researcher; Depthfirst names that flaw as Oracle's GraphQL interface, The Hacker News as Oracle REST Data Services. The chain was not independently reproduced.

CVE-2026-114938.exploitation_status: No exploitation in the wild reported as of 18 Nov 2026 (Rapid7, Red Hat). The finders, Calif, showed unauthenticated remote code execution against several popular Java applications and published a local test for vulnerable JDKs.
CVE-2026-114938.how_exploited: A heap buffer overflow (CWE-122, out-of-bounds write) in the hardware-accelerated Base64 decoder that the HotSpot JVM's optimising compiler substitutes on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI. When an application decodes attacker-supplied Base64 whose final group is malformed, the remaining-length calculation goes negative and the routine writes past the end of the output buffer. Java then rejects the input, but the heap corruption stays and can crash the JVM later. With further, application-specific work an attacker may turn it into code execution as the Java process, or read adjacent heap memory holding credentials, keys or session tokens (Red Hat).
preconditions: An affected runtime: OpenJDK 17 (17.0.6 and later per Red Hat), 21, 25 and 27 and builds based on them (Oracle Java SE, GraalVM, Red Hat and others), plus Oracle Java 8 Enterprise Performance Pack. Standard OpenJDK 8 and 11 lack the vulnerable code.

An x86-64 CPU with AVX-512 VBMI (Red Hat names Intel Ice Lake, Sapphire Rapids, Emerald Rapids, Granite Rapids and AMD Zen 4 to 6, including many cloud instance types). ARM64 and CPUs without AVX-512 VBMI are not known to be affected.
The JVM has the optimising compiler and the Base64 intrinsic enabled and is not limited to AVX2 or lower; Red Hat says no special or non-default configuration is needed.
The application passes attacker-controlled Base64 to the standard decoder, for example HTTP Basic credentials or tokens decoded before the login check; reachability must be confirmed per application.
Network access to that application; no authentication or user interaction is needed. Oracle rates attack complexity high (CVSS 8.1); Red Hat rates it low (9.8).
attack_path: Initial access: the attacker sends a request carrying malformed Base64 to an exposed Java service, typically in an authentication header or token that is decoded before any credential check.

Execution: repeated or shaped input corrupts heap objects next to the decode buffer; depending on application, JVM build and memory layout this can yield code running as the Java service account, or only a crash.
Impact: Red Hat notes adjacent heap data such as credentials, private keys and session tokens may be exposed; crashes may surface later, for example during garbage collection.
No in-the-wild intrusions, follow-on activity or attacker groups have been reported by Rapid7, Red Hat, CISA or Siemens as of 18 Nov 2026.
who_is_exposed: Internet-facing Java services on modern Intel or AMD x86-64 servers and cloud instances that decode Base64 credentials or tokens before authentication, such as web applications, API gateways and identity providers.

Products that bundle Java 17 or later: Red Hat lists Keycloak 26.4 and 26.6 and later and Single Sign-On 7.6 on OpenJDK 17; Siemens lists Industrial Edge Management Pro V1, V2 and Virtual (no fix yet).
Container images built on affected JDK base images, and appliances with an embedded Java runtime that does not appear as its own inventory entry (CISA).
Not exposed: ARM64 hosts, x86-64 CPUs without AVX-512 VBMI, and standard OpenJDK 8 and 11.
detect: Inventory: find every Java runtime, including ones bundled in applications, appliances and container images, and record vendor and full build number against the fixed releases (CISA, Rapid7).
Host CPU check: confirm whether each host reports the AVX-512 VBMI feature set; Red Hat lists the CPU flags that together make the path reachable.
Crash monitoring: watch for unexpected JVM crashes and fatal error logs on Java services (CISA), especially crashes in garbage collection or compiled code after unusual authentication traffic.

Process behaviour: alert on Java service processes starting shells or unexpected child processes, or making unusual outbound connections (CISA advises watching for suspicious Java processes and rogue runtimes).

Scanner coverage: Rapid7 published an authenticated check (content release 1.1.4115, 17 Nov 2026); Calif published a local test of whether a JDK is vulnerable. No indicators of compromise have been published.

steps: Inventory all Java runtimes, including bundled and containerised ones, and identify which run on hosts with AVX-512 VBMI.

Install Oracle's November 2026 Critical Security Patch Update or your OpenJDK distributor's fixed build, starting with internet-facing services that decode credentials or tokens before authentication.
Rebuild container images on patched base images, redeploy, and restart every Java process so the fixed runtime is actually loaded.
Apply updates from vendors of products that bundle Java (for example Siemens, Red Hat Keycloak) as they are released; until then use the vendor's mitigations.
Where patching must wait, apply an interim workaround below and limit unauthenticated access to affected services; remove the workaround after patching, as Red Hat advises.
fixed_versions: Oracle Java SE 8 Enterprise Performance Pack 8u513-perf
Oracle GraalVM for JDK 17 and 21 and GraalVM Enterprise 21: fixed builds in the November 2026 update
Other OpenJDK distributions and bundled runtimes: the distributor or product vendor patched release (Red Hat had not listed fixed packages on 18 Nov 2026)
Siemens Industrial Edge Management Pro V1, V2 and Virtual: no fix yet (SSA-272816)
workarounds: Restart the JVM with the HotSpot option that disables the Base64 intrinsic, which removes the vulnerable path while keeping other AVX-512 optimisations (Rapid7, Red Hat); apply it to every node and verify it on each running instance.
Alternatively limit the JVM to the AVX2 instruction level, which disables AVX-512 entirely (Red Hat); both workarounds apply to x86-64 only.
Restrict and validate Base64 input at the application boundary, enforce input size limits and limit unauthenticated access to affected services (CISA).
Siemens Industrial Edge Management: block direct internet access or shut the instances down until a fix is applied (Siemens).
verify: Confirm each running Java process, not just the installed package, reports a fixed build; restart anything still on the old runtime.
Rescan with an authenticated vulnerability check or the finders' local JDK test to confirm the runtime is no longer vulnerable.
Where a workaround is used, confirm on each running instance that the JVM actually started with it; Red Hat warns an environment variable alone is not enough.
if_compromised: Isolate the affected host or container and preserve JVM crash logs, application and web logs, and if possible a memory capture before restarting.
Rotate secrets the Java process held in memory, such as credentials, private keys, signing keys and session tokens, since heap contents may have been read.
Rebuild the service from a patched, known-good image rather than cleaning it in place, and check for new accounts or changes made under the service account.
Report the incident to your national CERT (in the US, CISA) and to the product vendor if a bundled runtime was involved.

CVE-2026-114938.caveats: Oracle's own advisory and the OpenJDK advisory refused automated readers (403), so Oracle details come from Rapid7's table, Red Hat, Siemens and CISA. Severity is disputed: Oracle and Siemens give CVSS 8.1 (high complexity), Red Hat 9.8. Rapid7 says reliable code execution needs significant extra, application-specific work; Red Hat says working exploits were shown in default configurations.

CVE-2026-115731.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild per CISA, which added it to KEV on 17 Nov 2026 citing evidence of active exploitation; no attacker or attack details have been published. Disclosed with fixes on 3 Nov 2026.
CVE-2026-115731.how_exploited: Deserialization of untrusted data (CWE-502) in the report-processing code of Puppet as used by Puppet Server. Agents send a report after each run, and events in it can carry a serialized Ruby object; the server rebuilds a type named in that data without enough checks. A client holding any CA-signed agent certificate submits a crafted report and runs arbitrary code on the Puppet Server as its service user. Red Hat notes this account can reach the certificate authority and every node the server manages.
preconditions: The attacker can reach the Puppet Server's agent-facing port over the network.
The attacker holds any CA-signed agent certificate, for example from a compromised managed node.
Where the certificate authority autosigns requests without strong verification, an unauthenticated attacker can obtain a certificate and needs nothing else.
Affected releases: Puppet Enterprise 2023.8.0 to before 2023.8.13, 2025.0.0 to before 2025.12.1, and 2026.0.0; open source Puppet and OpenVox servers before the 3 Nov 2026 fixes.
attack_path: Initial access: obtain an agent certificate, either by compromising any managed node or by requesting one from a CA that autosigns.
Execution: submit a crafted agent report to the server's report interface; the server deserializes it and runs code as the Puppet service user.
Privilege and reach: from the server, the attacker can read the CA signing key and change catalogs pushed to every managed node (Red Hat statement).
CISA has not said what attackers did next; plan for possible spread to all managed systems.
who_is_exposed: On-premises Puppet Enterprise primary servers and compilers on the affected release lines.
Open source Puppet Server and OpenVox Server before openvox-server 8.18.0 or 9.2.0 (Vox Pupuli says all known Puppet implementations are affected).
Red Hat Satellite environments, which process incoming client reports by default (Red Hat).
Any deployment with naive autosigning, or whose server port is reachable from untrusted networks or the internet.
detect: Version check: compare the Puppet Enterprise and bundled puppet-agent versions on primaries and compilers with the fixed releases.
Process telemetry: the Puppet Server Java process or Puppet service user spawning shells, interpreters or network tools.
Certificate authority: review recently signed or autosigned certificates for unknown node names, and any access to the CA key files.
Server and report logs: reports from unexpected nodes or with errors while processing events, and report submissions from addresses outside the managed estate.
Code and catalogs: unexpected changes to environments, modules or catalogs served to nodes after a suspicious report.

steps: Upgrade Puppet Enterprise to 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 or 2026.0.1 (bundling puppet-agent 8.22.2 or 9.1.3), or OpenVox to the fixed releases.
Restart Puppet Server after the upgrade so the fixed code is loaded (Perforce CVE record).
Disable autosigning or require strong verification for certificate requests.
Restrict network access to the Puppet Server so only managed nodes can reach it.
Review recently signed certificates and revoke any you cannot account for.
workarounds: Avoid autosigning certificate requests without strong verification, so untrusted clients cannot obtain an agent certificate (Red Hat).
Limit which network segments can reach the server (Vox Pupuli); this reduces exposure but does not fix the flaw.
verify: Confirm every primary server and compiler reports a fixed Puppet Enterprise release and that Puppet Server has been restarted since.
Confirm autosigning is off or policy-based, and the server port is not reachable from untrusted networks.
if_compromised: Isolate the Puppet Server and preserve logs, report data and disk images.
Treat the CA as compromised: rebuild the CA, reissue agent certificates and revoke the old ones.
Audit code, environments and catalogs for changes and check managed nodes for unexpected resources.
Rotate secrets held in Puppet data or reachable by the service user, rebuild from known-good media, and report the incident.

CVE-2026-115731.caveats: Perforce's advisory page did not load for an automated reader; vendor facts come from the CVE record Perforce published and from Red Hat and the OpenVox maintainers. CISA gives no detail on who exploited it or how. Exposure is internal for most sites, but servers reachable from the internet or with autosigning are open to anyone.

CVE-2026-116331.exploitation_status: Public exploit reported: Depthfirst researcher Zheng Yu published a working exploit on 18 Nov 2026 (Depthfirst, The Hacker News). No exploitation in the wild reported as of 19 Nov 2026. Fixed by PostgreSQL on 12 Nov 2026.
CVE-2026-116331.how_exploited: Type confusion in the PostgreSQL planner's min/max aggregate optimisation (PostgreSQL advisory). A logged-in user who can create objects defines a custom aggregate with a sort-operator option that makes the planner treat the aggregate's input and result as the same type when they are not, so a value of one type is read as another. Depthfirst describes turning this into an information leak, a memory read that defeats address randomisation and a control-flow hijack, ending in commands run as the operating-system account that runs the database.
preconditions: A database login that can create objects. Depthfirst notes that by default every role gets the TEMPORARY privilege through PUBLIC, which is enough to create the needed objects in its own temporary schema without any access to application tables.
Network access to the PostgreSQL port, or any application path that lets a user run arbitrary SQL under a database role.
attack_path: Initial access: the attacker logs in with any low-privilege database account (a stolen application credential, a reporting or analytics user, a tenant account on a shared server).
Staging: the attacker creates temporary objects, including a user-defined aggregate, in a temporary schema; no grants on application data are needed (Depthfirst).
Execution: queries using the aggregate trigger the type confusion, leak memory, defeat address randomisation and hijack control flow inside the server process (Depthfirst).

Impact: commands run as the database's operating-system user, giving access to all databases in the cluster, the data directory and credentials stored on the host. No post-exploitation activity has been reported.
who_is_exposed: Self-managed PostgreSQL servers on any supported branch below the fixed minor releases.
Servers where many people or applications hold logins: shared or multi-tenant clusters, analytics and reporting users, and databases whose port is reachable from the internet.
Managed PostgreSQL services until the provider rolls out the November 2026 minor releases; check the provider's own notice.
detect: Check every server's version against 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 and 14.25.
Review the PostgreSQL log (with statement or DDL logging enabled) for creation of user-defined aggregates or functions by accounts that normally never create objects, especially in temporary schemas.
Watch for PostgreSQL backend crashes and automatic restarts (server process terminated by a signal) in the server log, which can accompany failed attempts.
Look for shells or other unexpected child processes started by the postgres operating-system account, and for new files in the data directory or the account's home.
Neither PostgreSQL nor Depthfirst has published indicators or detection rules for this flaw.

steps: Upgrade to PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 or 14.25 or later; this is a minor update that needs no dump and reload or pg_upgrade, only replacing the binaries and restarting (PostgreSQL release announcement).
Read the release announcement's other post-update steps (index rebuilds and constraint checks for unrelated fixes) and any steps from earlier minor releases you skipped.
Plan to leave PostgreSQL 14: 14.25 is its final release, and PostgreSQL 13 is not listed among the fixed versions.
Until patched, and as hardening afterwards, revoke the default TEMPORARY privilege from PUBLIC on databases where ordinary roles do not need temporary tables (Depthfirst's advice).
Inventory database logins and remove or lock accounts that are not needed; rotate application credentials that are widely shared.
workarounds: PostgreSQL gives no workaround. The researcher advises revoking the TEMPORARY privilege that every role receives through PUBLIC; this reduces but may not remove the attack surface, since any role allowed to create objects elsewhere can still reach the flaw.
verify: Query the server version on each instance and confirm it is at or above the fixed minor release for its branch.
Confirm the running process was restarted after the binaries were replaced (server start time later than the upgrade).
If you revoked TEMPORARY, confirm that the privileges on each database no longer grant it to PUBLIC.
if_compromised: Isolate the database host from the network while keeping it running long enough to capture memory and process lists if your team can.
Preserve the PostgreSQL logs, the operating-system logs and a copy of the data directory before changing anything.
Rotate every database password and any secrets readable by the postgres operating-system account (replication credentials, backup keys, connection files).
Rebuild the host from a known-good image, restore data from a backup taken before the suspected compromise, and review other systems the database account could reach.
Report the incident to your national CERT or incident-response provider.

CVE-2026-116331.caveats: The vendor advisory and the researcher's write-up agree on the flaw and the impact. PostgreSQL's advisory names no workaround; revoking TEMPORARY is the researcher's advice only. The Hacker News reports the full chain was not independently reproduced. Managed-service patch timelines are set by each provider.
