CVE-2026-89103.exploitation_status: No exploitation reported: Onapsis, which found it (calling it PROXYGATE), said on 10 Nov 2026 it had not seen attacks. It demonstrated the attack end to end to SAP; no public exploit code is reported. Not in CISA's KEV catalog.
CVE-2026-89103.how_exploited: Incorrect authorization (CWE-863) in the SAP Gateway, the kernel component that handles RFC connections and can start programs on the host. SAP says the gateway activates its default access control list with high privileges, so an external attacker can be categorised as an internal application server. Onapsis says the flaw is in the gateway's CPI-C layer: where the proxy policy allows it, a crafted series of requests from an unauthenticated outsider makes the gateway believe the request comes from one of the system's own servers. Access lists that trust internal servers then allow it, and the gateway can run an operating system command as the SID-adm account.
preconditions: Network access to the SAP Gateway ports (33NN or 48NN) from the attacker's position.
A permissive proxy access list (prxyinfo), or no prxyinfo file and profile parameter gw/acl_mode_proxy left at its shipped value 0, which allows every proxy connection.
An affected kernel: 7.22, 7.53, 7.54, 7.77, 7.93, 8.04, 9.16, 9.20 or 9.21 below the fix, or an out-of-maintenance kernel.
No credentials or user interaction; hardened secinfo and reginfo lists do not stop it.
attack_path: Initial access: crafted gateway requests from an untrusted network make the gateway treat the attacker as an internal application server.
Execution: the gateway starts what the attacker asks for, in the worst case an operating system command as the SID-adm account (demonstrated to SAP; not seen in attacks).
Credential access, as Onapsis describes it: database credentials and secrets from the secure store and instance profiles, then direct reading or changing of business data.
Lateral movement and persistence: RFC destinations and technical credentials used to reach connected SAP and non-SAP systems; configuration or binaries changed to keep access.
who_is_exposed: Any system that runs an SAP Gateway: AS ABAP systems such as S/4HANA, ECC, BW and Solution Manager, AS Java and dual-stack systems, and standalone gateways.
Gateways with a permissive prxyinfo, at any patch level.
Gateways with no prxyinfo and gw/acl_mode_proxy not set to 1, which is the default for backward compatibility.
Gateways reachable from the internet directly, through a permissive SAProuter route or through partner connections are at highest risk.
detect: For every gateway, record whether prxyinfo exists and how broad its source and destination rules are, the gw/acl_mode_proxy value, kernel release and patch level, and which networks reach the gateway ports.
Review gateway logs and the dev_rd trace for proxy connections and program starts from hosts that are not the system's own application servers.
Look for unexpected processes started by the gateway or under the SID-adm account, and for logons and RFC calls from unusual sources in the Security Audit Log.
Check firewall and network logs for connections to ports 33NN and 48NN from outside the hosts that need RFC access. No public indicators of compromise exist.

steps: Find every gateway, including standalone gateways, AS Java and dual-stack systems, non-production copies and legacy systems.
Close permissive prxyinfo files first, starting with any gateway reachable from the internet; test in a non-production system because gateway-to-gateway scenarios may rely on proxy rules.
Where there is no prxyinfo, set gw/acl_mode_proxy to 1 on kernels that support it (7.93, 9.16 and kernels already at the fixed level); otherwise create a restrictive prxyinfo as an interim control.
Apply SAP Security Note 3798345: patch kernels 7.22, 7.53, 7.54, 7.77, 8.04, 9.20 and 9.21, then set gw/acl_mode_proxy to 1 where SAP requires it. Read FAQ Note 3810197.
Upgrade out-of-maintenance kernels to a supported downward-compatible kernel.
Apply the patch, the parameter and the prxyinfo change on every application server, not only the primary instance.
Block the gateway ports at the perimeter and limit them internally to hosts that need RFC access.
fixed_versions: Kernel 7.22 (EXT, EX2, EX3) patch level 1612 or later, plus gw/acl_mode_proxy set to 1
Kernel 7.53 PL 1625, 7.54 PL 718, 7.77 PL 915, 8.04 PL 244 or later, plus gw/acl_mode_proxy set to 1
Kernel 9.20 PL 16 and 9.21 PL 4 or later (no manual step listed)
Kernels 7.93 and 9.16: no new kernel needed; set gw/acl_mode_proxy to 1
workarounds: SAP lists no official workaround. Onapsis advises a restrictive prxyinfo, limited to trusted or internal-only sources, to reduce exposure until the patch is applied.
Restrict network access to the gateway ports to the hosts that need RFC access.
verify: Each application server's kernel is at or above the fixed patch level for its release.
gw/acl_mode_proxy shows the value 1 in the active profile of every instance, or a restrictive prxyinfo is loaded, and ideally both.
A kernel patch alone does not take a system out of scope; confirm the proxy policy as well.
Confirm from an outside network that the gateway ports cannot be reached.
if_compromised: Isolate the affected systems and preserve gateway logs, dev traces, the Security Audit Log and OS logs before changes.
Rotate database credentials, secure store entries, RFC destination passwords and technical user credentials.
Check connected SAP and non-SAP systems reachable over RFC for activity from the compromised system.
Rebuild or restore the SAP host from a known good state if commands ran as SID-adm, and report to your national CERT.

CVE-2026-89103.caveats: SAP's note is behind a login; fixed levels and the parameter step come from the finder's reading of Notes 3798345 and 3810197 and the public CVE record. Exploitation details are withheld. Exposure depends on configuration, so a version check alone cannot clear a system. Status could change; check KEV.

CVE-2026-89126.exploitation_status: No exploitation reported: Onapsis, which found it, said on 10 Nov 2026 (updated 12 Nov) it had not seen attacks. It gave SAP a private working exploit; no public exploit code is reported. Not in CISA's KEV catalog.
CVE-2026-89126.how_exploited: Heap-based buffer overflow (CWE-122) in the SAP kernel code that SAP Web Dispatcher shares with the ICM for reassembling fragmented WebSocket messages. An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the Web Dispatcher's HTTP or HTTPS port sends a crafted sequence of WebSocket messages, with invalid length fields in control frames, that makes the process write attacker-controlled data past its buffer. Depending on how it is shaped this either crashes the Web Dispatcher or corrupts memory in a controlled way, which Onapsis says lets the attacker run operating system commands as the SID-adm account that owns the SAP installation. The Web Dispatcher reassembles the messages itself, so the edge component is hit directly.
preconditions: Network access to the Web Dispatcher's HTTP or HTTPS port; Web Dispatchers are often internet-facing by design.
WebSocket support enabled, which is the default whether or not any application uses it.
A Web Dispatcher below the fixed patch level for its release (7.53, 7.54, 7.77, 7.93, 9.16, 9.18, 9.20), an affected HANA XS release, or an out-of-maintenance kernel from 7.40 on.
No login, user interaction or misconfiguration is needed.
attack_path: Initial access: crafted WebSocket traffic to the Web Dispatcher's web port corrupts its memory before any authentication.
Execution: operating system commands run as the SID-adm account (shown by Onapsis to SAP; not seen in attacks).
Impact without code execution: a single connection reliably crashes the Web Dispatcher, cutting off every SAP system behind it while it restarts; repeating keeps it down.

Likely next steps named by Onapsis for SID-adm access: reading database credentials and secrets from the secure store and profiles, collecting RFC destinations to move to connected systems, and changing configuration or binaries to persist.
who_is_exposed: Standalone SAP Web Dispatchers and Web Dispatchers embedded in AS ABAP kernels 7.53, 7.54, 7.77, 7.93, 9.16, 9.18 and 9.20.
The Web Dispatcher in SAP HANA 2.0 XS Classic and SAP Extended Application Services 1.0 (XS Advanced).
Out-of-maintenance kernels 7.40, 7.41, 7.42, 7.45, 7.49, 7.73, 7.81, 7.85 and 7.89, which may get no fix (Onapsis).
Not affected per Onapsis and RedRays: kernel 7.22 and SAP Content Server. The ICM in AS ABAP has the same bug under CVE-2026-76964.
detect: Inventory every Web Dispatcher, including small ones in front of HANA or third-party backends, and check its release and patch level on its admin page or in its startup log.

Investigate unexpected Web Dispatcher restarts in the dev_webdisp trace in the work directory and changes of its process ID outside maintenance; Onapsis says each attempt is likely to crash it at least once.
Review the Web Dispatcher HTTP log for WebSocket upgrades (status 101) from unexpected sources; the log must be switched on explicitly on release 7.54 and lower and in XS Classic.

Watch for unusual processes or file changes under the SID-adm account on Web Dispatcher hosts. RedRays has published network detection rules for this WebSocket flaw; no public indicators of compromise exist.

steps: Build the list of every Web Dispatcher: standalone, embedded in AS ABAP, and in HANA XS Classic and XS Advanced, plus non-production and legacy systems.
Patch internet-facing Web Dispatchers first by applying SAP Security Note 3778556 (SAPWEBDISP.SAR for standalone, dw.sar or the SP Stack Kernel for embedded instances); read FAQ Note 3778788.
Patch HANA XS Classic to the revision in the note and XS Advanced to the fixed runtime version.
Upgrade out-of-maintenance kernels to a supported downward-compatible kernel.
Apply Note 3778530 (CVE-2026-76964) to the ICM of every AS ABAP application server too; the same bug sits there.
Restrict the HTTP and HTTPS ports to the networks that need them while the rollout runs. RISE with SAP customers should read SAP Note 3849055.
fixed_versions: Kernel and Web Dispatcher 7.53 PL 1616 or 1617 and later; 7.54 PL 710; 7.77 PL 914; 9.16 PL 111; 9.18 PL 37; 9.20 PL 11 or 13 (Onapsis, from the SAP notes)
Kernel and Web Dispatcher 7.93: updated PL 401 Stack Kernel, PL 402, or PL 420 and later; PL 419 is still vulnerable
SAP HANA 2.0 XS Classic: revision 2.00.079.11 (SPS07) or 2.00.089.05 (SPS08)
SAP Extended Application Services 1.0 (XS Advanced): SP05 patch 4 (Onapsis); RedRays reads the note as version 1.5.4 or later
workarounds: SAP FAQ Note 3778788 (as described by Onapsis): turn off WebSocket upgrade support in the Web Dispatcher profile and restart it. This breaks ABAP Push Channels and some Fiori features, so first check the HTTP log for WebSocket upgrades.
Not using WebSocket does not protect a system; only disabling the support or patching does.
verify: Each Web Dispatcher's admin page or startup log shows a patch level at or above the fixed level for its release (for 7.93, one of the specific fixed levels, not just a higher number).
HANA XS Classic and XS Advanced report the fixed revision or version.
If WebSocket was disabled as a stopgap, confirm the profile change is active after restart, and record it as temporary.
if_compromised: Isolate the Web Dispatcher host and preserve its work directory traces, HTTP logs and system logs before restarting or rebuilding.
Rebuild the host from a known good state with a patched release rather than cleaning it in place.
Rotate secrets the SID-adm account could read: database credentials, secure store entries, certificates and keys, and RFC and technical user passwords.
Check backend SAP systems and connected systems for logons and changes from the Web Dispatcher host, and report the incident to your national CERT.

CVE-2026-89126.caveats: SAP's notes are behind a login; fixed levels and workarounds come from the public patch day page, the CVE record and the finders' and RedRays' readings of the notes. Exploitation details are withheld. Onapsis and RedRays differ slightly on the XS Advanced fix level. Status could change; check KEV.

CVE-2026-90436.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild: Rapid7 MDR saw it used against Confluence Data Center on 13 Nov 2026; N-able reported N-central exploitation the same day. Public PoC for N-central on 12 Nov. In CISA KEV since 18 Nov 2026.
CVE-2026-90436.how_exploited: Unsafe reflection (CWE-470) in Apache Axis 1.x, an end-of-life SOAP engine embedded in other products. When Axis processes an inbound SOAP fault, it loads and instantiates a class named inside the fault before checking its type; loading a suitable class already on the application's classpath runs attacker-influenced code. This happens while Axis resolves the target service, before any per-service handler, so service authentication does not help. An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the SOAP endpoint gains code execution as the host application's service account.
preconditions: The SOAP endpoint of an application embedding Axis 1.x (through 1.4) is reachable by the attacker; no authentication is needed.
Confluence Data Center: the Remote API (XML-RPC and SOAP) setting is enabled. It has been off by default for new installs since Confluence 3.0 and was removed in 10.0.
N-able N-central: the Legacy API feature is enabled (N-able says it is off by default).
Per Apache, code execution needs a suitable class on the application's classpath; the confirmed attacks on Confluence and N-central show those products are exploitable.
attack_path: Initial access: unauthenticated requests to the product's SOAP endpoint; in the Rapid7 case they returned server errors but still caused the Confluence Java process to start shell and download-tool processes within seconds.
Execution and discovery: hundreds of encoded commands (Rapid7 believes AI-assisted) enumerated the host, network, Confluence configuration and encryption keys.
Credential access: the attacker used Confluence's own database credentials to search pages, attachments and application links for passwords, tokens, VPN settings, private keys and card numbers.
Lateral movement: queried Atlassian Crowd for users and groups, tried AS-REP roasting against a domain controller (it failed), then used a harvested service account to query a cloud data warehouse.
Cloud access: about twelve hours in, signed in to Microsoft 365 as an integration service account using legacy authentication. Separately, crypto miners were reported on exploited N-central servers.
who_is_exposed: Confluence Data Center and Server up to 9.x (Atlassian lists affected releases through 9.5.4) with the Remote API enabled, unless on fixed release 9.2.28; Confluence 10.x and Atlassian Cloud are not affected.
On-premises and hosted N-central servers before 2026.4 HF3 with the Legacy API enabled.
Any in-house or third-party Java application that embeds Apache Axis 1.x through 1.4 and exposes a SOAP endpoint; Apache will not release a fix.
detect: Confluence access logs: unauthenticated POST requests to the SOAP endpoint, especially ones answered with server errors.
Process telemetry: the Confluence or N-central Java process spawning shells, interpreters or download tools under the service account.
Network: outbound connections from the application server to temporary tunnel services or unfamiliar hosts.
Database: logins with the Confluence database account from unexpected hosts or bulk reads of page, attachment and application-link tables.

Identity: legacy-authentication sign-ins to Microsoft 365 by service accounts, and Crowd or directory queries from the application; compare against the IOCs Rapid7 published (no match does not prove the host is clean).
Inventory: search code and installed products for Axis 1.x libraries to find other exposed applications.

steps: Find every system that embeds Axis 1.x, starting with Confluence Data Center and N-central, and check whether its SOAP or legacy API is enabled and reachable.
Confluence: upgrade to 9.2.28 or to 10.x; if that must wait, clear the Remote API (XML-RPC and SOAP) setting under General Configuration, which takes effect without a restart.
N-central: install 2026.4 HF3 (2026.4.1.39), confirm the Legacy API is disabled even on HF2, and follow N-able's agent and probe upgrade guidance.
Own applications on Axis 1.x: migrate to another SOAP engine such as Axis2/Java, or rebuild Axis with the patch from the fixing commit Apache names.
Restrict SOAP and API endpoints to trusted networks until patched, and treat exposed servers as emergency work outside normal patch cycles (Rapid7).
Hunt for signs of compromise on any server that was exposed before the fix.
fixed_versions: Confluence Data Center 9.2.28; Confluence 10.0 and later (Remote API removed)
N-able N-central 2026.4 HF3 (2026.4.1.39), which disables the Legacy API
Apache Axis 1.x: no fixed release; migrate or apply the upstream commit
workarounds: Confluence: disable the Remote API (XML-RPC and SOAP) setting; this may break integrations that use it.
N-central: keep the Legacy API disabled.
verify: Confirm the product version shows 9.2.28 or later (Confluence) or 2026.4.1.39 or later (N-central).
Confirm the Remote API or Legacy API setting is off and that the SOAP endpoint no longer answers from outside.
Re-run a software inventory scan to confirm no Axis 1.x library remains in exposed applications.
if_compromised: Isolate the server from the network but keep it running long enough to capture memory, logs and disk images.
Rotate the application's database password, application-link and Crowd credentials, service-account passwords and any secrets stored in pages or attachments.
Review Microsoft 365, cloud data warehouse and directory logs for use of harvested credentials, and block legacy authentication.
Rebuild the server from a known good image and restore only verified data.
Report the incident to your national CERT, and to CISA if you are a US federal agency under BOD 26-04.

CVE-2026-90436.caveats: Atlassian's issue page lists 9.2.28 as the fix and does not name fixed releases for 9.3 to 9.5; check Atlassian's full advisory for those lines. The Apache notice states no fixed Axis 1.x release will be made. Exploitation of other Axis 1.x products has not been reported.

CVE-2026-90817.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild according to CISA, which added it to KEV on 18 November 2026 (CISA's record rates exploitation active and automatable). No public attribution of this CVE to an actor. Disclosed 20 September 2026 by Securifera.
CVE-2026-90817.how_exploited: Code injection (CWE-94) combined with external control of a file name or path (CWE-73) in REDCap. An unauthenticated attacker who holds a valid public survey link manipulates requests so that the public survey context reaches a controller route it should not, then supplies a crafted file path or stream value to the Data Import handling. That lets the attacker run arbitrary code on the REDCap web server, with access to the application, its database credentials and research data.
preconditions: REDCap 13.3.0 or later, before 16.0.49 LTS, 17.3.10 LTS or 17.4.4 Standard Release.
The REDCap web application is reachable by the attacker; no login is needed.
The attacker knows a valid public survey hash, which is present in any public survey link that has been shared or published.
attack_path: Initial access: crafted requests from a public survey link reach the Data Import handling and execute code on the REDCap server.
Execution: code runs as the web server account that hosts REDCap.

Likely next steps (from GTIG's report on earlier REDCap intrusions, not tied to this CVE): harvesting database and service credentials, planting a web shell, and trojanizing REDCap files to steal logins and survive upgrades.
who_is_exposed: Universities, hospitals and research institutions that self-host REDCap 13.3.0 or later and publish public surveys.
Institutions that leave older REDCap version folders installed beside the current one (GTIG warns these enable downgrade attacks).
detect: Version check: compare the REDCap version in the Control Center with the fixed releases, and list every REDCap version folder on the server.
Web server logs: public survey requests that reach Data Import functions or carry unusual file path values, especially from unauthenticated sessions.
Process telemetry: the web server process spawning shells or interpreters, as suggested by vulnerability trackers.
File integrity: unexpected PHP files in the web root and changes to REDCap's upgrade, authentication and hook files; scan with the YARA rule GTIG published for INFINITERED.
Database: unusual entries in REDCap's sessions table and unexpected administrator accounts.

steps: Upgrade to REDCap 16.0.49 LTS, 17.3.10 LTS or 17.4.4 Standard Release or later, as applies to your track.
Remove old REDCap version folders left on the server after earlier upgrades.
Until patched, restrict access to the REDCap server to trusted networks where your surveys allow it.
Check the server for signs of compromise, as required for US federal agencies under BOD 26-04 forensic triage.
Rotate REDCap database and service account passwords if the server was exposed while unpatched.
verify: Confirm the version shown in the REDCap Control Center is a fixed release or later.
Confirm no older REDCap version folders remain in the web root.
Confirm file integrity of REDCap's core files against a fresh copy of the same release.
if_compromised: Take the REDCap server off the network and preserve web logs, the database and a disk image.
Treat every credential that passed through the server as exposed: rotate database, service and user passwords and enforce two-step verification for administrators.
Rebuild from a clean REDCap release and restore only verified data.
Review email and identity systems for misuse of harvested credentials, including mail forwarding rules.
Report the incident to your national CERT; research data breaches may also need regulator notice.

CVE-2026-90817.caveats: The vendor's notice is on the REDCap Community site, which needs a partner login, so it was not read; fixed versions come from the CVE record by the finder (Securifera) and CISA's catalog. The Securifera write-up did not load. GTIG's June 2026 report on UNC6508 REDCap intrusions names no CVE and is used only for post-compromise context.

CISA adds four KEVs, 18 Nov 2026

CVE-2026-91609.exploitation_status: No exploitation in the wild reported as of 20 Nov 2026 (CISA SSVC: none). On 18 Nov 2026 Depthfirst reported a chain with CVE-2026-114819 giving code execution; not independently reproduced.
CVE-2026-91609.how_exploited: A flaw in the GraphQL component of Oracle REST Data Services (ORDS), the HTTP layer that exposes Oracle Database objects as web services. Oracle's CVE record describes it as easy to exploit by an attacker with a low-privileged account and network access over HTTP, letting them read critical data or all data ORDS can reach (confidentiality only, CVSS 6.5). Depthfirst reports that, chained with the Oracle Text flaw CVE-2026-114819, an attacker who can reach only the exposed web endpoint can deliver a crafted document into the database and run commands on the database server as its operating system service user, before any database login. Neither Oracle nor the researcher has published the flaw class in detail.
preconditions: Oracle REST Data Services 24.2.0 to 26.2.1 (the versions Oracle's CVE record lists) without the October 2026 Critical Patch Update.
The ORDS HTTP endpoint, including its GraphQL interface, is reachable by the attacker.
On its own, Oracle rates the flaw as needing a low-privileged account; the researcher says the chain with CVE-2026-114819 needs no login.
For the code-execution chain, the backing Oracle Database is also unpatched for CVE-2026-114819 (fixed in Oracle's November 2026 update).
attack_path: Initial access: the attacker reaches the ORDS web endpoint over HTTP, from the internet or an internal network.
Abuse of the GraphQL interface to read data ORDS can reach (Oracle's description), or as the first link in the researcher's chain.

Execution (researcher's chain): a crafted document is passed into the database and processed by Oracle Text code affected by CVE-2026-114819, giving command execution as the database's operating system service user.
No post-compromise activity has been reported, because no attacks have been seen; an attacker with that access could read or change all database data and move to other systems.
who_is_exposed: Organisations running Oracle REST Data Services 24.2.0 to 26.2.1, whether standalone, in an application server, or in front of APEX or other applications.
Deployments that publish ORDS or its GraphQL interface to the internet or to broad internal networks.
Highest risk: the same estate also runs Oracle Database 19c, 21c or 23 without the November 2026 update (CVE-2026-114819).
detect: Inventory: check the ORDS version on every server and container; anything from 24.2.0 to 26.2.1 is affected.
ORDS and front-end web server or load balancer access logs: GraphQL requests from unexpected sources, unusual volumes, or accounts that normally do not use GraphQL.
Oracle Database audit trail: unexpected Oracle Text index activity or document loads linked to ORDS connection users.
Database host: new processes started by the Oracle service account, unexpected outbound connections from the database server, and new files in Oracle directories.
No indicators of compromise or detection rules have been published by Oracle or the researcher as of 20 Nov 2026.

steps: Find every ORDS installation and its version, including ones bundled with APEX or run in containers.
Apply the Oracle REST Data Services update from Oracle's October 2026 Critical Patch Update (released 20 Oct 2026).
Apply Oracle's November 2026 update to Oracle Database to close CVE-2026-114819, the other half of the reported chain.
Until patched, limit who can reach ORDS: put it behind a VPN, reverse proxy or allow list, and do not expose the GraphQL interface publicly unless it is needed.
Review which database schemas and accounts are enabled for ORDS and remove those that are not needed.
fixed_versions: Oracle REST Data Services: the release delivered by Oracle's October 2026 Critical Patch Update (versions 24.2.0 to 26.2.1 are affected per Oracle's CVE record)
verify: Confirm each ORDS instance now reports a version later than 26.2.1, from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update.
Confirm the backing Oracle Database has the November 2026 update applied.
Rescan with your vulnerability scanner and confirm CVE-2026-91609 and CVE-2026-114819 no longer appear.
if_compromised: Isolate the ORDS server and the database host from the network while keeping them running for evidence.
Preserve ORDS and web server logs, database audit trails and host logs before changing anything.
Rotate database account passwords, ORDS connection credentials, OAuth client secrets and any secrets stored in the database.
Rebuild affected hosts from known-good images and restore data from backups taken before the suspected compromise.
Report the incident to your national CERT and, if personal data was exposed, to your data protection authority.

CVE-2026-91609.caveats: Oracle's October 2026 advisory and blog returned 403 to automated readers, so this analysis uses Oracle's text as carried in the CVE record (NVD and CVE.org) rather than the advisory itself. Oracle rates the flaw as needing a login and affecting confidentiality only; the researcher says the chain with CVE-2026-114819 needs no login and runs code. The chain was not independently reproduced, the flaw class is undisclosed, and whether GraphQL is enabled by default was not confirmed.

CVE-2026-96652.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild: Plex (19 Oct 2026 update) says the chain is actively and widely exploited after a public proof of concept appeared on 16 Oct 2026; CISA added it to KEV on 20 Oct 2026. No actor named.
CVE-2026-96652.how_exploited: Server-side request forgery (CWE-918) in the player timeline function of Plex Media Server before 1.43.3.10861. The server accepts any value as the access token on this function and does not check that a protocol parameter is only a protocol name, so a remote attacker can make the server send requests to a destination of their choosing, including the server itself on loopback. Because Plex trusts local traffic, this is the entry point of the Plex2Shell chain: with CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655 and CVE-2026-96656 it leads to theft of the owner token and code execution as the Plex service account.
preconditions: The Plex Media Server is reachable by the attacker, typically because Remote Access is on or the Plex port is forwarded to the internet.
The server runs a version before 1.43.3.10861.
No real account is needed: any token value is accepted on the vulnerable function (NVD and CISA scores rate it low privilege; SonicWall and Plex treat it as unauthenticated).
attack_path: Initial access: the attacker makes the server send a request on their behalf, reaching services bound to loopback that Plex trusts without authentication.
Credential access: through the related URI injection flaw (CVE-2026-96654) the attacker gets the server to reveal the highly privileged owner token (SonicWall).

Execution: with the owner token, the file-write flaw (CVE-2026-96656) plants a malicious library in the Codecs folder, which Plex loads unsigned when a stream starts, running code as the service account.
Impact seen by Plex: compromised servers were used to run cryptocurrency miners and proxy software.
who_is_exposed: Self-hosted Plex Media Server installs on any platform older than 1.43.3.10861 with Remote Access enabled or the service port forwarded to the internet.
Servers reachable only on a home or office network are exposed to anyone on that network.
Anything the Plex service account can reach (mounted shares, credentials on the same machine or VM) is at risk once the chain completes (Plex).
detect: Check the version under Settings, General in Plex Web; anything below 1.43.3.10861 is vulnerable, and Plex says internet-reachable servers below it should be treated as possibly compromised.
Look for unfamiliar processes started by Plex Media Server, especially proxy-, miner- or random-looking names; Plex's advisory lists example names.
Look for unfamiliar shared library files in the Plex Codecs folder and transcoder options in Preferences.xml you did not set.
Watch for outbound connections to the proxy-streaming domain named in Plex's advisory, and sustained high CPU use when nothing is playing.
SonicWall IPS signatures 22567, 22568 and 22569 cover the SSRF, file-write and URI-injection stages.

steps: Update Plex Media Server to 1.43.3.10861 or later on every install, and update Plex Desktop to 1.115.0 or later.
Until updated, turn off Remote Access if it is not needed and stop forwarding the Plex port directly from the internet.
Check every server that was internet-reachable on an older version for the signs Plex lists before trusting it again.
If any sign is found or compromise cannot be ruled out, follow the if-compromised steps below.
workarounds: Turn off Remote Access under Settings if it is not needed (Plex).
Avoid forwarding the Plex service port directly to the internet (Plex).
SonicWall suggests a reverse proxy that strips or validates the protocol parameter, and perimeter IPS signatures; these are not vendor fixes.
verify: Plex Web shows version 1.43.3.10861 or later under Settings, General on every server.
No unexpected processes, Codecs-folder libraries or transcoder preference entries remain after the update.
if_compromised: Rebuild from a clean installation rather than reusing the old Plex data directory; at minimum clear the Codecs folder and review Preferences.xml (Plex).
Sign out all devices in the Plex account settings and change the Plex password.
Treat mounted shares and any credentials on the same machine or VM as exposed, and rotate them.
Preserve logs and a copy of the suspicious files before cleaning, and report to your national CERT if it is an organisation's server.

CVE-2026-96652.caveats: Plex's own forum notice and SonicWall agree on the chain, but sources differ on whether this flaw needs authentication (NVD and CISA score low privilege because any token value works) and on its score (5.3 on NVD, 8.6 from SonicWall). No victim count or actor is published, and the original researcher's write-up was not read.

CVE-2026-96654.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild as part of the four-flaw Plex2Shell chain: details public 16 Oct 2026, attacks recorded from 17 Oct; Plex confirmed widespread attacks and CISA added it to KEV on 20 Oct 2026. No actor named.
CVE-2026-96654.how_exploited: Improper neutralization of encoded URI schemes (URL injection) in a Plex Media Server search function. Plex says the flaw exposes internal agent functions that should only be reachable from the server itself; The Hacker News says a crafted value lets an attacker call other plugins' functions with parameters of their choosing. In Plex2Shell it is reached through an unauthenticated server-side request forgery (CVE-2026-96652) and is used to obtain the server owner's admin token, which unlocks the file-write flaw that gives code execution.
preconditions: Plex Media Server older than 1.43.3.10861.
The attacker can reach the server's default port, usually through Remote Access or manual port forwarding; internal-only servers are exposed to anyone on that network (Field Effect).
In the observed chain, the companion request-forgery flaw CVE-2026-96652 is used to reach these loopback-only functions; no valid credentials are needed.
No user interaction is needed.
attack_path: Initial access: an unauthenticated server-side request forgery makes the server send requests to itself.
Privilege gain: this flaw lets those requests call internal agent functions with attacker-chosen parameters, which is used to obtain the owner's admin token.
Staging and execution: with the token, CVE-2026-96655 fetches an attacker file and CVE-2026-96656 writes it into the Codecs directory, where Plex loads and runs it.
Follow-on: attackers installed an XMRig-based cryptocurrency miner and a backdoor that doubles as a reverse proxy (The Hacker News, Plex).
who_is_exposed: Self-hosted Plex Media Server installations before 1.43.3.10861 on any platform, including NAS devices and virtual machines.
Servers with Remote Access enabled or the Plex port forwarded; Shadowserver counted more than 36,000 unpatched internet-reachable servers in early September 2026 (Field Effect).
Installs that do not update automatically, especially NAS packages (Field Effect).
detect: Check the version in Plex Web under Settings, General; anything older than 1.43.3.10861 is vulnerable.
Review your Plex account's signed-in devices and access for sessions you do not recognise, since the stolen owner token gives full control.

Look for the later stages of the chain: unfamiliar library files in the Codecs folder, transcoder settings you did not set, and unknown child processes of Plex (Plex advisory names the processes seen).
Watch for sustained high CPU while idle and outbound connections from the Plex host to unknown hosts.
Use the Plex2Shell detection rules and packet captures researchers published (referenced by Field Effect).

steps: Check exposed servers for signs of compromise first; patching does not remove files, processes or a token already stolen (Field Effect).
Update Plex Media Server to 1.43.3.10861 or later on every install.
Turn off Remote Access if not needed and avoid forwarding the Plex port directly.
Sign out of all devices and change the Plex password on servers that were exposed while vulnerable, so any stolen owner token stops working.
Inventory all Plex deployments, including NAS units and remote workers' servers (Field Effect).
workarounds: Disable Remote Access if it is not needed (Plex).
Avoid forwarding port 32400 directly to the internet unless needed (Plex).
verify: Plex Web, Settings, General shows 1.43.3.10861 or newer.
The account's device list shows only your own devices after signing everything out.
if_compromised: Isolate the host and keep logs, the Codecs folder and the preferences file as evidence.
Rebuild Plex from a clean install rather than reusing the old data directory (Plex).
Sign out of all devices, change the Plex password, and rotate credentials for shares the service account could reach.
Federal agencies: follow CISA's BOD 26-04 forensic triage requirements and report the incident.

CVE-2026-96654.caveats: Sources describe this flaw differently: Plex calls it access to internal agent functions over the loopback interface, The Hacker News calls it URL injection in a search endpoint that leaks the admin token, and the Plex post does not say what access is needed to reach it alone. That the request-forgery flaw is what reaches the loopback-only functions is inferred from how the sources describe the chain. Its danger comes from the chain, not from the flaw alone.

CVE-2026-96655.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild as part of the Plex2Shell chain: Plex (19 Oct 2026) says the chain is widely exploited after a public proof of concept on 16 Oct 2026; CISA added it to KEV on 20 Oct 2026. No actor named.
CVE-2026-96655.how_exploited: Server-side request forgery (CWE-918) in the universal transcode function of Plex Media Server before 1.43.3.10861: an authenticated user can make the server request arbitrary internal or external addresses (NVD, CISA). That lets an attacker use the server to reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints it can see. Plex's own notice lists this CVE as exposure of the server owner's admin token. CISA says it can be chained with CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654 and CVE-2026-96656 to reach code execution as the Plex service account.
preconditions: The Plex Media Server is reachable by the attacker, typically through Remote Access or a forwarded Plex port.
The server runs a version before 1.43.3.10861.
The attacker has a valid token for the server; in the chain this comes from the unauthenticated SSRF (CVE-2026-96652) and token theft stages.
attack_path: Initial access: the attacker enters through CVE-2026-96652 and the related flaws, which let outside requests be treated as local.

Discovery and credential access: this flaw lets the attacker make the server fetch internal or external addresses of their choosing, including internal services and cloud metadata (NVD, SonicWall); Plex describes the outcome as exposure of the owner's admin token.
Execution: with the owner token, the file-write flaw (CVE-2026-96656) plants a malicious library in the Codecs folder, which runs when a stream starts.
Impact seen by Plex: miners and proxy software running on compromised servers.
who_is_exposed: Self-hosted Plex Media Server installs older than 1.43.3.10861 with Remote Access on or the service port forwarded.
Servers in cloud VMs, where requests to the metadata service can expose instance credentials.
Internal services reachable from the Plex host, which become reachable to the attacker through it.
detect: Check the version under Settings, General in Plex Web; below 1.43.3.10861 is vulnerable.
Look for outbound requests from the Plex host to internal addresses or the cloud metadata service that Plex has no reason to make.
Look for unfamiliar processes started by Plex, unfamiliar libraries in the Codecs folder and transcoder options in Preferences.xml you did not set (Plex lists examples).
Watch for connections to the proxy-streaming domain named in Plex's advisory and high CPU use when nothing is playing.
SonicWall IPS signatures 22567, 22568 and 22569 cover stages of the chain.

steps: Update Plex Media Server to 1.43.3.10861 or later on every install, and Plex Desktop to 1.115.0 or later.
Until updated, turn off Remote Access if it is not needed and stop forwarding the Plex port from the internet.
On cloud hosts, review what the instance role or metadata credentials can do and limit them.
Check every server that was internet-reachable on an older version for signs of compromise before trusting it again.
workarounds: Turn off Remote Access under Settings if it is not needed (Plex).
Avoid forwarding the Plex service port directly to the internet (Plex).
verify: Plex Web shows version 1.43.3.10861 or later on every server.
No unexpected processes, Codecs-folder libraries or transcoder preference entries remain.
if_compromised: Rebuild from a clean installation instead of reusing the old Plex data directory; at minimum clear the Codecs folder and review Preferences.xml (Plex).
Sign out all devices in the Plex account settings and change the Plex password, which also invalidates the exposed owner token.
Rotate cloud instance credentials and any secrets on shares or the same machine the Plex account could reach.
Preserve logs and suspicious files first, and report to your national CERT if it is an organisation's server.

CVE-2026-96655.caveats: Sources disagree on what this CVE is: NVD, CISA's catalog and CSAF describe an authenticated SSRF in the transcode function, while Plex's notice lists it as disclosure of the owner's admin token; no source explains the difference. Exploitation is reported for the chain as a whole, not for this flaw on its own. No actor or victim count is public.

CVE-2026-96656.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild as the last step of the four-flaw Plex2Shell chain: details public 16 Oct 2026, attacks from 17 Oct; Plex confirmed widespread attacks; CISA added it to KEV on 20 Oct 2026. No actor named.
CVE-2026-96656.how_exploited: External control of file name or path (CWE-73) in Plex Media Server's transcoder preferences. Someone holding the server owner's administrator token can set a transcoder option that makes the server write a file of their choosing into its Codecs directory. Plex loads shared libraries from that directory, so a planted library runs with the privileges of the Plex service. In Plex2Shell, attackers first obtain the admin token and make the server fetch their file through the other three flaws, so the whole chain needs no valid credentials.
preconditions: Plex Media Server older than 1.43.3.10861.
The attacker can reach the server's default port, usually through Remote Access or manual port forwarding; servers reachable only internally are exposed to anyone on that network (Field Effect).
Administrator rights on the server; in the observed attacks this came from the owner token leaked by CVE-2026-96654 and CVE-2026-96655 rather than stolen credentials.
The server can make outbound connections to an attacker-controlled host so the file to be written can be fetched (Field Effect).
attack_path: Initial access: an unauthenticated server-side request forgery (CVE-2026-96652) and a URL injection (CVE-2026-96654) are used to obtain the owner's admin token.
Staging: with the token, a second request forgery (CVE-2026-96655) makes the server download a file from the attacker.
Execution: this flaw writes that file as a shared library into the Codecs directory via transcoder settings, and Plex loads it, running attacker code as the Plex service account.
Follow-on: attackers ran a shell script that installed an XMRig-based cryptocurrency miner and a backdoor that also works as a reverse proxy (The Hacker News, Plex).
Impact: CPU theft, the victim's network used to relay third-party traffic, and access to whatever shares, backups or credentials the service account can reach (Field Effect).
who_is_exposed: Self-hosted Plex Media Server installations before 1.43.3.10861 on Windows, Linux, macOS, NAS devices and virtual machines.
Servers with Remote Access enabled or the Plex port forwarded to the internet; Shadowserver counted more than 36,000 unpatched internet-reachable servers in early September 2026 (Field Effect).
NAS appliances and other installs that do not update automatically (Field Effect).
Servers on home or remote-worker networks used for work, and servers sharing a network with business systems.
detect: Check the version in Plex Web under Settings, General; anything older than 1.43.3.10861 is vulnerable.
Look for unfamiliar shared-library or DLL files in the Plex Codecs folder, and for transcoder options in the preferences file you did not set (Plex).
Look for unrecognised child processes of Plex Media Server; Plex's advisory names three process names seen in attacks.
Watch for sustained high CPU while nothing is playing, and for outbound connections from the Plex host to unknown hosts, including the domain Plex's advisory names.
Use the detection rules and packet captures researchers published for Plex2Shell (referenced by Field Effect) for threat hunting.

steps: Before patching, check exposed servers for the signs of compromise above, because the update does not remove files, processes or settings planted earlier (Field Effect).
Update Plex Media Server to 1.43.3.10861 or later on every install, including NAS packages and remote users' servers.
Turn off Remote Access under Settings, Remote Access if it is not needed, and stop forwarding the Plex port directly unless required.
Inventory every Plex deployment across servers, NAS units, virtual machines and remote workers (Field Effect).
Limit what the Plex service account can reach, such as file shares, backups and management interfaces.
workarounds: Disable Remote Access if it is not needed (Plex).
Avoid forwarding port 32400 directly to the internet unless needed (Plex).
verify: Plex Web, Settings, General shows 1.43.3.10861 or newer.
The Codecs folder holds only files Plex installed, and the preferences file has no transcoder options you did not set.
An external scan no longer finds the server reachable if Remote Access was turned off.
if_compromised: Isolate the host and preserve logs, the Codecs folder and the preferences file before cleaning.
Rebuild Plex from a clean install rather than reusing the old data directory (Plex); at minimum clear the Codecs folder and reset transcoder options.
Sign out of all devices in your Plex account and change the Plex password, which invalidates the stolen owner token.
Treat shares and stored credentials the service account could reach as exposed: rotate them and check them for misuse.
Federal agencies: follow CISA's BOD 26-04 forensic triage requirements and report the incident.

CVE-2026-96656.caveats: Plex's advisory does not state the authentication requirement for each flaw separately; the administrator requirement comes from the CVE description and The Hacker News. Sources disagree on the KEV date (20 or 21 Oct) and the patch date (3 or 4 Aug). Reddit reports of the same miner may not all come from this chain (The Hacker News).

CVE-2026-96951.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild: Microsoft marked it 'Exploitation Detected' when it released the fix on 13 Oct 2026 (not publicly disclosed beforehand); CISA added it to KEV the same day. No actor named; Tenable says a link to APT28 is unconfirmed.
CVE-2026-96951.how_exploited: Command injection (CWE-77) in Windows Shell that Microsoft classes as a security feature bypass of Mark of the Web. The attacker sends a specially crafted file by email or instant message, or lures the user to a site that delivers it. When the user opens it, the warnings, Protected View and blocking that Mark of the Web normally applies to downloaded files are skipped, so whatever the file launches runs without the usual prompt. Microsoft scores it 8.8 with high impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability.
preconditions: The target user opens or clicks an attacker-supplied file or link; Microsoft says the attacker cannot force this.
The machine runs a Windows client or server build older than the October 2026 security update (or an Edge version before 154.0.4258.62).
No account on the target is needed; the attacker only has to get the file to the user.
attack_path: Delivery: a crafted file arrives as an email attachment, chat or collaboration message, or download from an attacker's site (Microsoft, Help Net Security).
Defence evasion: opening the file bypasses Mark of the Web, so Windows shows no security warning or Protected View.
Execution: content the attacker chose runs in the user's session without the prompt that would normally stop it.
Follow-on activity has not been described publicly; Tenable notes two earlier exploited Windows Shell flaws this year, one linked to APT28.
who_is_exposed: All supported Windows client versions (Windows 10 1607 to 22H2, Windows 11 23H2 to 26H2) before the October 2026 update.
Windows Server 2012 R2, 2016, 2019, 2022 and 2025, including Server Core, before the October 2026 update.
Users who receive outside email, chat or downloads; Microsoft also lists Edge and Outlook.com as affected, fixed on Microsoft's side or by updating Edge.
detect: Check build numbers against Microsoft's fixed builds (for example Windows 11 24H2 at 26100.9711 or later, Windows Server 2022 at 20348.5761 or later).

Look for files from email, chat or the web that ran without a Mark of the Web prompt: Explorer or Office starting script hosts, installers or unexpected child processes right after a user opened a downloaded file.
Review mail and web gateway logs for unusual attachments or container files delivered to users who then showed suspicious process activity.
No indicators of compromise or detection rules have been published by Microsoft or CISA for this flaw.

steps: Install the October 2026 Windows security update on every client and server; CISA's federal deadline was 16 Oct 2026.
Update Microsoft Edge to 154.0.4258.62 or later.
Confirm that machines reached the fixed build, starting with those whose users handle outside email and downloads.
Because the flaw was exploited before the fix, check machines that opened untrusted files in the weeks before patching for signs of compromise; CISA's catalog sets forensic triage for this entry.
verify: The OS build on each machine is at or above the fixed build Microsoft lists for its version.
Your update management tool reports the October 2026 cumulative update as installed and the machine has rebooted.
if_compromised: Isolate affected machines and preserve memory, disk and email evidence before cleaning.
Reset passwords and sessions of users on those machines and review their account activity.
Rebuild machines where unknown code ran, then patch before reconnecting.
Report the incident to your national CERT; US federal agencies follow CISA's forensic triage requirements.

CVE-2026-96951.caveats: Microsoft's advisory is brief: it does not say which file types are used, who exploited the flaw or since when. Help Net Security adds no technical detail beyond the delivery routes. Reports disagree on whether functional exploit code is public and whether this is linked to APT28; Microsoft's CVSS temporal vector marks exploit code as functional. KB numbers were not confirmed from Microsoft, so fixed builds are given instead.

CVE-2026-97229.exploitation_status: Exploited in the wild per CISA, which added it to KEV on 29 Oct 2026 (federal deadline 1 Nov 2026). GitLab's 12 Oct 2026 release notes reported no exploitation at disclosure. No actor has been named publicly.
CVE-2026-97229.how_exploited: Integer overflow in the regular-expression compiler (Onigmo, the engine shipped with GitLab's Ruby) used for CI/CD rules. A crafted pattern in a CI configuration slips past GitLab's length and repeat checks, so the compiled program grows beyond a 32-bit size and the size check passes on the wrapped value. A later jump calculation is then wrong, and execution moves into attacker-controlled data. Rapid7 showed this leads to arbitrary commands running as GitLab's git operating-system account.
preconditions: Self-managed GitLab CE or EE 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5, or 19.4 before 19.4.2; GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already patched.
The GitLab web interface or API is reachable by the attacker.

GitLab rates it as needing no privileges, but Rapid7's demonstrated route needed a malicious CI configuration pushed to a public project (project write access) and then an unauthenticated CI lint request against that commit.
attack_path: Staging: the attacker places a CI configuration with a hostile regular expression, and a specially named file path, in a project the server will evaluate.
Initial access: the attacker asks the CI lint feature to evaluate that commit; for a public project this needs no credentials (Rapid7).
Execution: the overflowed regex program corrupts memory in the Ruby worker and runs attacker-chosen commands as the git system account.
Follow-on: as the git account the attacker can reach repository data, CI secrets and server configuration; no post-exploitation activity has been published for this CVE.
who_is_exposed: Self-managed GitLab CE and EE servers on the affected 19.2, 19.3 and 19.4 lines, especially those reachable from the internet.
Instances with public projects or open sign-up, where outsiders can push or evaluate CI configuration, fit the route Rapid7 described.
Other Ruby applications that compile regular expressions from untrusted input are exposed to the underlying Onigmo bug until Ruby is upgraded (Ruby project).
detect: Check the installed GitLab version on every self-managed instance against the fixed releases 19.2.8, 19.3.5 and 19.4.2.

Deploy GitLab's six published threat detections for self-managed instances (Onigmo native worker crash, GraphQL CI lint hostile regexp, oversized non-ASCII path, regexp guard rejection, Workhorse worker crash, scripted client error burst).
Correlate long-running CI lint requests ending in gateway errors with Puma worker crashes or restarts and sudden jumps of about 2 GiB in worker memory (Rapid7).
Look for shell or other unexpected child processes started by GitLab Ruby workers running as the git account.
Review recently pushed commits in public projects for unusual regular expressions in CI rules and multi-byte path names.

steps: Upgrade every self-managed GitLab instance to 19.2.8, 19.3.5 or 19.4.2 or later for its release line.
Until patched, restrict credential-free access to public projects that outsiders can write to, or block the CI lint endpoint at the proxy (Rapid7); this does not fix the compiler itself.
Because CISA lists it as exploited, check each instance for signs of compromise from before the patch, as BOD 26-04 expects.
Upgrade Ruby to 3.3.13, 3.4.12 or 4.0.9 or later on other systems that run Ruby applications compiling untrusted patterns.
workarounds: Rapid7: restrict unauthenticated access to writable public projects or block the CI lint endpoint as a temporary measure; GitLab itself lists no workaround other than upgrading.
verify: Confirm the version shown on the instance's help page or admin area matches a fixed release.
Confirm GitLab's threat detections are deployed and that no worker crash alerts follow the upgrade.
if_compromised: Isolate the server and preserve logs, memory and disk images before rebuilding.
Rotate secrets the git account could read: CI/CD variables, runner registration tokens, deploy keys, access tokens and integration credentials.
Rebuild on a fixed release from known-good backups and review repositories and pipelines for tampering.
Report the incident to your national CERT (in the US, CISA).

CVE-2026-97229.caveats: The privilege needed is disputed: GitLab says no privileges, but Rapid7's route needed project write access and the original report is private. CISA has not said who exploits it or how widely. GitLab's advisory gives no post-compromise guidance; the steps above are general practice.
